By enabling rapid screening of candidate probes, the proposed framework reduces the reliance on routine post-fabrication SEM characterization and shortens the nanoprobe development cycle, thereby improving experimental efficiency and enhancing the scalability of TERS probe development.

title: Theory-driven and AI-empowered inverse design of metasurfaces
abstract: The lack of physical constraints in metasurface inverse design often leads to inefficient exploration of high-dimensional spaces and to designs difficult to realize physically. We propose an automated inverse design framework integrating physical theory with reinforcement learning. The Equivalent Circuit Model (ECM) not only provides a high-performance initial structure but also reconstructs the solution space by compressing infinite geometric space into a finite, physically meaningful parameter domain. These physical constraints are maintained throughout optimization, ensuring all explorations remain within physically realizable bounds. A real-time closed loop between the RL agent and a full-wave simulator is established hierarchically. Q-learning optimizes macroscopic parameters, followed by Hierarchical Proximal Policy Optimization (HPPO) for microscopic topological refinement. Physical and manufacturing constraints are embedded into both the action space and reward function, improving simulation-to-fabrication consistency. An ultra-wideband absorbing metasurface designed with this framework achieves over 90% absorption from 2.9 to 17.2 GHz (relative bandwidth 143%) under normal incidence, with excellent polarization insensitivity and continuous absorption up to 60 oblique incidence. Measured results agree well with simulations. This theory-guided, hierarchically optimized, constraint-embedded framework provides a new pathway for metasurface inverse design. • A theory-guided inverse design framework is established, where physical theory serves as a solution space reconstructor rather than merely an initial structure generator. • Macroscopic parameter optimization via Q-learning and microscopic topological refinement via hierarchical proximal policy optimization (HPPO) are synergistically integrated within a single reinforcement learning loop. • Manufacturing constraints including minimum feature size and connectivity are directly embedded into the reward function, ensuring simulation-to-fabrication consistency without post-processing. • The proposed hierarchical strategy effectively reduces search complexity and escapes local optima in high-dimensional discrete design spaces, achieving a 12% bandwidth improvement beyond conventional topology optimization. • An ultra-wideband absorbing metasurface is designed and fabricated, exhibiting over 90% absorption from 2.9 to 17.2 GHz (relative bandwidth 143%) with excellent polarization insensitivity and stable performance up to 60 oblique incidence.

title: Interpretable attention framework for materials property prediction and mechanistic discovery
abstract: Machine learning in materials science is often limited by black-box predictions and scarce experimental data, which hinder reliable discovery and mechanistic understanding. Here we present SEAM, a self-explaining attention network that embeds interpretability directly into model architecture rather than relying on post-hoc analysis. SEAM records physically meaningful information during prediction through attention mechanisms and integrates multi-method cross-validation using attention analysis, integrated gradients, and SHAP to ensure robust interpretation. Specifically, Bayesian optimization enables automatic adaptation, achieving a predictive accuracy of R 2 = 0.84 for the ductility of molybdenum-based refractory alloys. By distinguishing causal mechanisms from spurious correlations, SEAM reveals a critical “correlation inversion” for Tungsten: while statistically correlated with high ductility, decoupling analysis identifies W as an intrinsic embrittler. This is validated by complementary first-principles calculations showing Re-induced bond softening versus W-induced stiffness preservation. This integrated framework bridges data-driven prediction with physical understanding, enabling trustworthy learning and rational design in data-scarce and mechanistically complex materials systems.

title: Inverse design of high-entropy superalloys using machine learning and generative artificial Intelligence
abstract: • End-to-end inverse design yields decision-grade HESA shortlists from data. • Creep (LMP) and oxidation ( log K A ) are optimized as first-class objectives. • Composition-only, physics-informed surrogates with descriptor and outlier control. • Feasibility floor + Pareto + Ward-medoids deliver a diverse experimental shortlist. • Conditional VAE explores new alloys under feasibility and sustainability filters. We introduce a structure-agnostic inverse-design workflow that turns heterogeneous literature and database evidence into experiment-prioritized shortlists of high-temperature high-entropy superalloy candidate chemistries. Unlike most data-driven high-entropy alloy (HEA) design studies that optimize a small set of proxies, we provide an end-to-end, reproducible decision-support loop that treats high-temperature creep and oxidation as first-class objectives and outputs compact shortlists for downstream validation. From curated multi-source data, we learn structure-agnostic, physics-informed surrogate models for the key high-temperature objectives – creep resistance (Larson–Miller parameter), oxidation kinetics (parabolic rate constant), melting point, density and elastic properties – and map predictions to “desirability” normalized scores. Candidate alloys are screened by a uniform feasibility floor and Pareto non-domination, then compressed by Ward–medoid clustering to yield compact, diversity-preserving shortlists for downstream validation. To explore beyond brute-force enumeration under the same admissibility rules, we couple the screening stage to a constraint-conditioned variational autoencoder, and retain only generated candidates that pass the full surrogate stack. The resulting compressed Pareto sets extend the occupied property envelope of legacy Ni-based superalloys while remaining interpretable through elemental-role analyses and Ashby-style trade-off maps. An external thermodynamic plausibility cross-check further shows that higher microstructure-oriented scores enrich the candidate space in single-phase HEA-compatible chemistries with wider stability windows and more favorable transition classes. Finally, we show how the same pipeline can be restricted to sustainability-compatible element pools, enabling performance-aware exploration under supply-risk and footprint constraints.

title: Inverse design of a thermally self-adaptive carbon fiber acoustic metastructure using a residual MLP architecture
abstract: To address the dual challenges of low-frequency and broadband noise mitigation in variable-temperature aerospace environments, this study proposes an intelligent inverse design framework that integrates a deep residual multilayer perceptron (Res-MLP) surrogate model with a genetic algorithm (GA) optimizer. The resulting thermally self-adaptive carbon-fiber acoustic metastructure (TS-CFAM) employs embedded shape memory alloy (SMA) actuators to convert ambient thermal stimuli into controlled mechanical displacement, thereby enabling real-time reconfiguration of its resonant microarchitecture and overcoming the fixed-bandwidth limitation inherent to conventional passive acoustic metamaterials. Numerical and experimental results confirm that the Res-MLP surrogate model accurately captures the high-dimensional, strongly nonlinear acoustic–thermal–mechanical coupling, achieving a test-set coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.99. Validation further demonstrates that TS-CFAM delivers a continuous thermal frequency-tuning range of 1240 Hz—spanning 620 Hz to 1860 Hz—over the 30–50 °C operational range. Under weighted multi-objective optimization, the framework attains a 14.23% reduction in total structural mass and a 33.30% decrease in radial thickness, while sustaining an average sound absorption coefficient above 0.88 across the target band. Collectively, this work establishes a scalable, physics-informed digital design paradigm for structural–functional integration in next-generation aviation noise-mitigation systems.

title: Non-invasive drug-release monitoring via AI-enhanced ultrasound in gelatin-magnesium gallate hydrogels
abstract: • Non-invasive monitoring of drug release from Gelatin-Magnesium Gallate hydrogels • Machine learning enables high-accuracy analysis of hydrogel acoustic signals. • Validated our strategy in varied dispersion medium and cell culture conditions. • Drug release-induced hydrogel degradation resulted in acoustic impedance variation. Hydrogel-based drug delivery systems have been actively explored for precision and personalized medicine, leveraging their localized, sustained, and biocompatible approach for drug administration. However, conventional platforms generally lack real-time monitoring capabilities, as therapeutic evaluation typically relies on invasive or end-point analyses. While stimuli-responsive hydrogels offer controlled release, non-invasive strategies to track in vivo release kinetics is still challenging. We addressed these limitations using an acoustic system coupled with a deep learning framework to analyze ultrasound (US) signal variations from a gelatin-magnesium gallate (GMG) hydrogel, thereby demonstrating the feasibility of non-invasive, time-dependent drug release monitoring. A machine-learning framework quantitatively decodes subtle acoustic variations, enabling non-invasive monitoring with > 95% accuracy. GMG hydrogel was fabricated using highly porous magnesium gallate MOFs (metal–organic frameworks), and the drug (gallic acid) release-mediated structural changes in the hydrogel were observed through US signal variations. Drug release was validated under diverse experimental conditions to ensure reproducibility of the results. Integration of US with AI-based analysis demonstrates the potential for non-invasive, real-time monitoring of drug release from hydrogel-based systems by analyzing the complex pattern of US signals and maintaining hydrogel integrity that enables insight into structural changes during drug release.

title: Data-driven discovery of roughness descriptors for surface characterization and intimate contact modeling of unidirectional composite tapes
abstract: Unidirectional tapes surface roughness determines the evolution of the degree of intimate contact required for ensuring the thermoplastic molecular diffusion and the associated inter-tapes consolidation during manufacturing of composite structures. However, usual characterization of rough surfaces relies on statistical descriptors that even if they are able to represent the surface topology, they are not necessarily connected with the physics occurring at the interface during inter-tape consolidation. Thus, a key research question could be formulated as follows: Which roughness descriptors simultaneously enable tape classification—crucial for process control—and consolidation modeling via the inference of the evolution of the degree of intimate contact, itself governed by the process parameters? . For providing a valuable response, we propose a novel strategy based on the use of Rank Reduction Autoencoders (RRAEs), autoencoders with a linear latent vector space enforced by applying a truncated Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to the latent matrix during the encoder-decoder training. In this work, we extract useful roughness descriptors by enforcing the latent SVD modes to (i) accurately represent the roughness after decoding, and (ii) allow the extraction of existing a priori knowledge such as classification or modelling properties. • Data-driven framework based on a Rank Reduction AutoEncoder (RRAE) to extract latent descriptors of surface roughness in unidirectional composite tapes. • A limited number of features enables accurate roughness reconstruction, surface classification, and prediction of intimate contact evolution. • Improved robustness and accuracy compared to standard machine learning and statistical approaches. • Strong potential for process optimization and real-time control in composite forming.

title: Machine learning in laser welding of electric vehicle batteries: Process control and quality assurance
abstract: Laser welding serves as a pivotal technology for ensuring the structural integrity and electrical connectivity of electric vehicle (EV) battery packs, which directly influences product safety and mass production consistency. However, the inherent non-linearity of process dynamics, compounded by the limitations of traditional open-loop control and lagging offline inspection, presents significant challenges to achieving zero defect manufacturing. Emerging machine learning technologies offer a transformative data-driven paradigm to address these bottlenecks by enabling real-time monitoring and intelligent decision-making. This paper presents a systematic review of machine learning applications in battery laser welding and categorizes them into two core domains, including intelligent process control and smart quality assurance. For process control, the review discusses the transition from passive monitoring to active adaptation through multimodal sensing, parameter optimization and reinforcement learning-based closed-loop adjustment. Regarding quality assurance, the paper analyzes strategies for real-time defect diagnosis and the quantitative prediction of key mechanical and electrical properties, and explores the prospective correlation between welding process signatures and battery lifecycle performance. Furthermore, the review critically examines current challenges, including industrial data scarcity, model generalization and system integration. Finally, it highlights future directions such as physics-informed neural networks and digital twin technologies to realize the vision of intelligent manufacturing of EV batteries.

title: Automated distillation of composition–processing–structure–performance linkages from fragmented and multi-modal materials literature
abstract: • A dual-pipeline framework enables large-scale extraction of structured linkages from materials literature through heterogeneous table parsing and hierarchical text mining. • 31,833 structured composition–processing–structure–performance linkages are distilled from 10,098 articles across 7,600+ alloys, yielding a database whose scale substantially exceeds that of the source literature • Improve token efficiency by ∼43% and 94.52% extraction fidelity through automated anomaly detection and ground-truth validation. • Hidden Processing–Structure–Performance relationships are uncovered via knowledge graphs and statistical patterns, enabling accurate prediction across diverse alloy systems. Decades of materials genome remain locked in fragmented multi-modal literature, and existing data-mining techniques struggle to reconstruct Composition–Processing–Structure–Performance (intrinsic and service performance) chains. Herein, we developed DualTrack-MatExtractor, the dual-pipeline framework integrating rule-based natural language processing with large language models for heterogeneous table parsing and text mining. Leveraging high-throughput semantic parsing, it distills 31,833 structured C–P–S–P linkages from 10,098 full-text articles across 7,600 alloys, generating datasets far exceeding the scale of the source literature. It achieves ∼43% higher token efficiency than purely LLM-based methods and a 94.52% extraction F1-score through automated anomaly detection. Distilled knowledge is validated through two pathways: Processing-route knowledge graphs with distributions of PFZ width, yield strength, and corrosion Icorr, reveal processing–structure–property relationships previously buried. Application to representative alloy systems further demonstrates predictive capability: for Cu-Ni-Sn, semantic co-word networks enables a physics-informed neural net-work prediction of strength-conductivity with 92% accuracy; for Al-Zn-Mg-Cu, a DeepSeek-Math-7B–assisted symbolic regression enables strength–ductility synergy (Q-index) prediction with an R-squared of 93.60%, far exceeding the standalone model (41.12%); for high-entropy alloys, 1,340 extracted samples train a neural network achieving 95.9% accuracy in phase-structure prediction. Overall, DualTrack-MatExtractor offers a scalable and high-fidelity pathway for materials data mining and AI-enabled materials design.

title: A neural network-based hardening model for plastic anisotropy evolution in a face centered cubic material
abstract: This study presents a data-driven approach for modelling the hardening behavior of polycrystalline materials using artificial neural networks (ANNs) integrated within a crystal plasticity (CP) framework. A dataset of slips and hardening parameter combinations was extracted from crystal-level simulations. This dataset contained some contradictory points where similar inputs produced significantly different outputs, and a filtering process was introduced to selectively eliminate these points for aiding the neural network to better capture representative data. Multiple ANN architectures were evaluated, with a network comprising 5 hidden layers identified as the most accurate for predicting the work hardening behavior. The final model was implemented as a hardening rule in the CP model. The ANN outperformed the Voce hardening rule with stress prediction errors reduced to below 2%. Texture evolution, stress-strain curves, and strain ratios were also analyzed across different material orientations for uniaxial and plane strain tension. Despite some limitations, such as strain ratio predictions, the proposed model shows significant promise. It offers improved predictive accuracy in stress-strain curves, providing a viable alternative to traditional hardening functions in CP modeling. This work highlights the potential of well-trained neural networks to effectively capture the complex, non-linear hardening behavior of polycrystalline materials.

title: Linking early stages viscous flow sintering mechanics to elastic properties in silica glass: A multiscale DEM-FEM framework
abstract: Understanding the interactions between processing, microstructure, and properties during sintering is required for designing materials with tailored functionalities. This study validates a Discrete Element Method (DEM) model for viscous flow sintering of silica glass, focusing on microstructural evolution and effective elastic property prediction. Microstructures at various sintering stages were reconstructed in 3D using neural networks applied to FIB-SEM imaging. A quantitative comparison between the DEM-simulated microstructures and these 3D reconstructed microstructures confirm the model’s robustness to capture densification. The validated DEM microstructures were employed as Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) for Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations to compute the effective Young’s modulus. The numerical predictions align with experimental measurements for the intermediate sintering stage (relative density > 0.8). The stiffness overestimation observed during the initial consolidation phase (relative density < 0.7) is attributed to the continuous representation of the granular network and boundary condition effects. This coupled DEM-FEM methodology bridges discrete particle-level mechanics with macroscopic material performance, providing a predictive framework to assist the mechanical design of sintered materials.

title: Recent progress on mechanical reinforcement of silica aerogels and their applications
abstract: Silica aerogels possess a unique nanoporous network and outstanding properties such as ultralow density and thermal conductivity, making them attractive for aerospace, building energy conservation, and environmental remediation. However, their inherent brittleness, low mechanical strength, and poor fracture toughness severely restrict practical applications. Enhancing mechanical performance while retaining excellent thermal insulation therefore remains a major challenge. This review summarizes recent progress in mechanically reinforced silica-based aerogels from three aspects: architectural design, multiphase compounding, and molecular engineering. Freeze casting, additive manufacturing, and aerogel fiberization are discussed as architectural strategies for constructing ordered, continuous, and anisotropic skeletons. Organic polymers, inorganic fibers or whiskers, and carbon nanomaterials are reviewed as reinforcing phases, with emphasis on multiscale synergy and interface engineering. Molecular-level approaches, including precursor regulation and chemical crosslinking, are also analyzed for improving network connectivity and flexibility. The applications of reinforced silica aerogels in adsorption and separation, acoustic absorption, fire-resistant insulation, and flexible sensing are further outlined. Finally, future directions, including bioinspired hierarchical design, intelligent manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted development, are proposed to guide the design of thermally insulating yet mechanically robust silica aerogels.

title: Inverse design of personalized textiles with architected curved yarns
abstract: Textiles are widely used materials with high mechanical tunability arising from their hierarchical architecture. Recent advantages in additive manufacturing enable precise, yarn-level fabrication that allows control of yarn topology and fabrication of personalized textiles with architected curved yarns with a programmable mechanical response. Yet, both the forward and inverse design of these textiles remains challenging due to the large design space and the nonlinear, globally coupled mechanical behavior due to yarn connectivity. Here, we present on a new class of personalized textiles that are weaves with architected curved yarns and an inverse design framework for them that combines a compact Artificial Neural Network (ANN) representation of yarn orientation, a streamline-based weave generator, a calibrated simulation, and a gradient-based optimization method utilizing an ANN surrogate. Together, the inverse design framework enables the optimization of high-dimensional, personalized textile structures that are tailored to produce a target response using significantly fewer simulations than state-of-the-art methods. The proposed framework is experimentally validated and is shown to solve several inverse design problems, from stress-shielding textiles to shape morphing. These results demonstrate that data-efficient, surrogate-driven optimization can satisfactorily navigate within the design space of architected textiles, paving the way for automated, personalized design of functional textiles.

title: Inverse design of acoustic topological insulators based on physics-informed neural network
abstract: Research on acoustic topological insulators has advanced, with their topologically protected edge states enabling dissipationless sound transmission and showing potential in anti-interference acoustic devices and communication. However, precise and efficient design remains a challenge due to the complexities of geometric configurations and the sporadic nature of phase transitions. This study proposes a Topological-evaluation Network, a physics-informed neural network framework that integrates physical band structure information into the network as an embedding structure. Through convolutional operations for feature separation, it enables the inverse design and mechanistic analysis of acoustic topological insulators. A symmetry-related Core and Perturbation Design Strategy was discovered through this framework. Compared to traditional trial-and-error methods based on numerical simulation, this strategy simplifies the acquisition of acoustic structures with topological insulation properties. It effectively optimizes the design efficiency for systems with complex physical mechanisms. By integrating physical band information, the framework achieves a 12-fold reduction in training data volume. The proposed model achieves a 95 % prediction accuracy in identifying topological phases, significantly accelerating the design of complex acoustic insulators. This approach offers extensive applications for future analysis and design of complex acoustic topological systems.

title: Explainable machine learning reveals orbital design rules for reversible H2 adsorption on single-atom-doped TiO2 nanoparticles
abstract: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier for decarbonized technologies, but reversible on-board storage remains challenging because efficient uptake and release under near-ambient conditions require a narrow adsorption-energy window. Here, we combine high-throughput electronic-structure calculations with explainable machine learning to uncover the governing factors of molecular hydrogen adsorption on single-atom-doped TiO 2 nanoparticles. Screening 30 dopants across perpendicular and parallel H 2 adsorption geometries reveals substantial variation in adsorption strength and clear configuration-dependent behavior. From a broad descriptor space, a three-stage feature-selection strategy identifies eight robust predictors, which are further reduced through symbolic regression to an analytical and interpretable model. The resulting descriptor space is governed by H–H activation, dopant–H 2 distance, and -electron rearrangement. Adsorption within the target window is associated with balanced -donation and -back-donation, with Group 4 and 5 transition metals emerging as the most robust candidates across geometries. Combined with Langmuir-based desorption estimates, these results provide a mechanism-based screening rule for reversible hydrogen storage on doped TiO 2 .

title: Multi-model machine learning framework for predicting material properties of BaTiO3-based ferroelectric ceramics
abstract: Predicting multiple functional properties of ferroelectric ceramics simultaneously remains challenging due to complex nonlinear interactions between composition, processing conditions, and microstructural evolution. This study presents a unified machine learning framework for predicting four key properties of BaTiO 3 ceramics: piezoelectric coefficient ( ), dielectric constant ( ), dielectric loss tangent ( ), and density ( ). The framework integrates an in-house experimental dataset from ten independent fabrication runs, augmented to 10,000 instances using Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Networks (CTGAN), with statistical fidelity validated through KL divergence and Wasserstein distance analyses. Domain-specific features comprising compositional ratios, dopant-site descriptors, and processing parameters are synthesized to capture nonlinear structure–property relationships. A consensus-based feature selection strategy combining Random Forest importance and SHAP values confirms that all fourteen engineered descriptors carry meaningful predictive information. Seven models comprising three baselines (Linear Regression, Random Forest, SVR) and four gradient boosting algorithms (AdaBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) are benchmarked using Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and five-fold cross-validation. CatBoost achieves the highest performance across all targets, with of 0.922 for , 0.933 for , 0.855 for , and 0.674 for . Ablation studies confirm that domain-specific feature synthesis contributes approximately 38 percentage points of improvement, establishing a reproducible and interpretable pipeline for multi-property prediction in ferroelectric ceramics.

title: A self-heating-based physics-guided neural network for fatigue life prediction of polymer matrix composites
abstract: Great efforts have been made to obtain accurate and reliable fatigue life models for polymer matrix composites (PMCs) that encompass their complexity in a short time frame. This investigation employs a physics-guided neural network (PGNN) with self-heating behavior embedded as soft physics constraints to predict the fatigue life of different PMCs reported in the literature. Due to the limited data size, which ranges from 12 to 21 samples, Monte-Carlo simulations were used to generate synthetic data (up to 1000 samples) that adhere to the distribution of the experimental data. Comprehensive k-fold cross-validation is performed by varying k from 2 up to leave-one-out (LOOCV) on the proposed PGNN architecture to ensure robust prediction and generalization. This model was applied to four distinct PMCs subjected to cyclic loading under stress ratios (R = -1 and R = 0.1) and cyclic frequencies (5, 10 and 50 Hz). The results demonstrate that stabilized surface temperature can predict fatigue life within a factor of two, maintaining reasonable accuracy even for materials that exhibit scatter up to a factor of four. Ultimately, this framework can successfully guide early-stage material screening phase for structural design of PMCs, even when the available experimental data is scarce.

title: Machine learning–assisted grain boundary segmentation reveals nanoscale heat treatment behavior of additively manufactured 316L stainless steel
abstract: Additive manufacturing produces inhomogeneous and anisotropic microstructures that differ from those in conventionally processed materials. Heat treatment is a crucial process to regulate the microstructural properties. Although estimating the resultant microstructure is a challenging issue, visualizing grain boundaries (GBs) would provide fundamental understanding of the mechanism during heat treatment. In this study, we developed a visualization method using electron diffraction mapping in transmission electron microscopy combined with machine learning. By extracting the area where the feature of electron diffraction patterns varies in the mapping data, GB region was successfully visualized. The developed image processing was applied to ex-situ heating observation of an additively manufactured 316L stainless steel (316L SS), and the curvature variation of GB before and after heat treatment was discussed. It is shown that existing sub-GBs likely attracts GBs, causing unevenness in GB migration.

title: Enhancing corrosion rate prediction under data scarcity with virtual sample generation and heterogeneous transfer learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of corrosion rates is essential for optimizing the alloy composition of structural metals and evaluating their service lifetimes. However, corrosion datasets for newly developed structural metals are typically of limited size, and significant differences in alloy composition, environmental conditions, and data dimensionality between existing and new material datasets often prevent direct knowledge reuse. In this paper, we propose a structural metal corrosion rate prediction framework that combines virtual sample generation and heterogeneous transfer learning (VSG-HTL). We first apply three topology-based virtual sample generation strategies to augment the limited training data and compare their effectiveness. We then utilize heterogeneous transfer learning to transfer knowledge from large-scale corrosion datasets of existing materials to the new dataset, selecting appropriate fine-tuning strategies based on the similarity between datasets. Experiments on multiple structural metal corrosion datasets under different environmental conditions demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms a baseline artificial neural network and other existing methods in predictive accuracy, validating its effectiveness in scenarios with limited samples and heterogeneous data.

title: FracFlowFormer: Generative forecasting of microstructural evolution in thermal barrier coatings
abstract: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) during thermal-shock durability testing of thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) is limited to a few checkpoints, which limits microstructural evolution analysis due to sparse imaging data. Here we present FracFlowFormer, a data-efficient forecasting framework that learns from limited early-stage SEM observations and predicts late-stage fracture and pore evolution in TBCs. To address the issue of coarse temporal sampling, we reconstruct more densely sampled temporal sequences employing TV-L1 dense optical-flow interpolation, thereby generating intermediate states that maintain fracture- and pore-relevant morphology. FracFlowFormer forecasts subsequent microstructural evolution using a hybrid architecture that combines a U-Net encoder–decoder and a spatio-temporal fusion transformer for long-range temporal SEM image generation, enabling high-fidelity predictions that capture microstructural evolution in TBCs during thermal-shock cycling, with 89.95% SSIM, 0.049 LPIPS, and 23.18 dB PSNR. An optical-flow branch provides a microstructural evolution cue that complements grayscale appearance and temporal aspects information. The framework reconstructs high-fidelity, time-resolved image sequences from sparse early-stage observations and demonstrates descriptor-based characterization of microstructural evolution, thereby transforming TBC characterization from static inspection into evolution-aware analysis of degradation and failure.

title: Interpretable transfer learning accelerates the design of high-temperature-resistant copper alloys with limited data
abstract: Copper alloys are critical for high-temperature applications, including rocket combustion chamber linings and nuclear reactor deflectors, yet traditional smelt-cast alloys struggle under extreme thermal conditions. Recent advances in big data and machine learning have enabled the efficient design of high-performance copper alloys. Here, we propose a novel interpretable transfer learning model–the electrical conductivity-hardness artificial neural network (ECH–ANN)–that integrates feature and model transfer to accurately predict properties of dispersion-strengthened copper alloys via powder metallurgy. We further established a feature screening pipeline comprising correlation screening, recursive elimination, recursive addition, and exhaustive screening. Using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), we quantified the importance and impact of key features on performance. Guided by these insights, a high-performance Cu-5.0 vol% Cr 2 O 3 composite was designed and fabricated through in-situ internal oxidation, achieving a strength of 570 MPa, electrical conductivity of 73.6 % IACS, and a softening temperature of 1000 °C, approaching copper’s melting point. This work provides a data-efficient framework for designing advanced materials, while elucidating the relationships between component characteristics and material properties.

title: Neural inverse design of self shaping composites
abstract: Self-shaping fiber-reinforced polymer ( FRP ) sheets offer a moldless method for generating complex 3D geometries by leveraging internal stresses. This innovative process enables sustainable fabrication of curved forms but presents a challenging inverse design problem: determining the fiber orientations that will produce a desired geometry. A data-driven approach is introduced for the inverse design of self-shaping FRP sheets, leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks ( CNNs ) trained on a large synthetic dataset generated from physically informed simulations. Two strategies are evaluated: (i) a direct prediction model that predicts fiber layouts from target surfaces, and (ii) an optimization method based on a trained surrogate model. The models are validated against physical prototypes and integrated into the Grasshopper design environment, facilitating accessible use within design workflows. It is demonstrated that the direct prediction model offers rapid, accurate predictions within the training distribution, while the optimization method generalizes better and is able to approximate freeform geometries. This work highlights the potential of machine learning to streamline moldless fabrication processes for complex architectural components.

title: Derivative-free optimization for crystal plasticity parameter calibration: benchmarking, non-uniqueness, and transferability
abstract: Crystal plasticity (CP) models are widely used to describe anisotropic deformation in metallic materials, yet their predictive capability relies on accurate calibration of numerous material parameters. This calibration task constitutes a high-dimensional, computationally expensive black-box optimization problem strongly affected by prior parameter uncertainty. Here, CP parameter calibration is formulated as a budget-constrained optimization problem, and four derivative-free algorithms, namely Nelder-Mead, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Bayesian Optimization, are benchmarked under a unified protocol. Three representative CP models are considered: a BCC phenomenological model, an FCC dislocation-density model, and an HCP slip-twinning model. Performance is evaluated by minimum normalized root-mean-square error under a fixed evaluation budget across narrow, medium, and wide prior domains. Bayesian Optimization shows the highest sample efficiency and robustness under wide priors and complex landscapes, whereas Genetic Algorithm provides the most stable surrogate-free baseline. Nelder-Mead performs satisfactorily only in low-dimensional settings with restricted priors. Calibration difficulty is governed primarily by parameter-error landscape structure rather than nominal dimensionality: FCC under wide priors is the most challenging regime, whereas the higher-dimensional HCP model remains tractable. Low fitting error does not guarantee parameter identifiability because near-optimal regions may involve substantial parameter trade-offs.

title: Disordered metamaterials and network architectures: towards sustainability‑by‑design and functional applications
abstract: With the growing interest in synthetic and advanced materials for sustainable applications, there is increasing demand for design‑driven, multifunctional performance from metamaterials and architected networks. While metamaterials are typically periodic, introducing controlled disorder as a sustainability‑by‑design strategy can enhance functionality compared to ordered architectures, enabling application‑focused structure–property optimization with improved resource efficiency and durability. The rapid integration of artificial intelligence and data‑driven materials design is driving a new paradigm in materials‑by‑design, where machine learning facilitates efficient exploration of complex design spaces. This perspective examines emerging materials and design approaches for disordered metamaterials, emphasizing structure–processing–property–performance relationships relevant to materials sustainability. It highlights potential for vibration attenuation, acoustics, wave control, and tailored mechanical behavior. The advantages of these periodic counterparts are critically discussed from the perspectives of reliability, robustness, and environmental sustainability. Recent studies show disordered architectures can deliver enhanced mechanical performance, including auxeticity, high stiffness‑to‑weight, impact resistance, reduced brittleness, and superior attenuation, while being less dependent on strict symmetry and more tolerant to defects, supporting sustainable manufacturing. Consequently, disordered metamaterials emerge as damage‑tolerant, performance‑oriented sustainable systems offering superior responses under realistic conditions. The article reviews advanced manufacturing routes, summarizes the state of the art, and outlines future directions for data‑enabled, life‑cycle‑informed design compatible with circular economy objectives.

title: Prediction of segregation, short-range order, and plasticity in nickel based polycrystals: insights from an uncertainty aware machine learning potential
abstract: Trace phosphorus segregation at grain boundaries (GBs) offers a promising yet insufficiently quantified route to strengthen multicomponent nickel-based superalloy (NBS), where segregation, chemical short-range order (CSRO), and plasticity are intrinsically coupled. Here, we develop a quinary moment tensor potential for Ni-Cr-Fe-Al-P and validate its accuracy and transferability. Uncertainty quantification based on maximum‑volume and D‑optimality criteria is further employed to assess the reliability of the potential during polycrystalline segregation and tensile simulations. Hybrid MC/MD simulations reveal a temperature-driven transition in phosphorus segregation, from uniform GB segregation at 300 K to Cr 3 P-rich amorphous complexions localized at triple junctions at 1000 K. Uniaxial tension on the segregated models further identifies a CSRO-controlled strengthening baseline together with an additional morphology-dependent segregation strengthening associated with enhanced dislocation pinning, pile-ups, and sessile dislocation formation. These results highlight the potential for predictive segregation engineering in NBS.

title: Physics-inspired feature engineering and interpretable machine learning for thermoelectric properties of multicomponent materials
abstract: Machine learning can accelerate thermoelectric materials discovery, yet most models remain “black boxes” lacking physical insight. We present an interpretable framework coupling Extra Trees regression with SHAP analysis to predict electrical conductivity (EC), Seebeck coefficient (SC), and thermal conductivity (TC) across 3879 multicomponent compositions. Physics-inspired feature engineering expands descriptors to 73–84 per target via polynomial lattice-distortion terms, cross-interactions, and compositional disorder statistics. Random-split test-set values reach 0.961, 0.965, and 0.958 for EC, SC, and TC, respectively, surpassing a lightweight deep neural network. Composition-wise splitting reduces to 0.822, 0.871, and 0.876, indicating limited generalisation to unseen compositions. SHAP analysis reveals property-specific associations: elemental descriptors dominate all targets, lattice-distortion terms influence EC, and heavy-element features affect TC. As a consistency check, a ZT-proxy computed from the independently predicted transport properties agrees reasonably well with experimental values on the test set ( = 0.84); it is intended as a screening aid rather than a verified figure of merit. This interpretable framework supports screening and prioritisation backed by, not replacing, experimental validation.

title: Reinforcement learning for inverse silhouette design and rapid laser cutting of compact parallelogram quad kirigami prototypes
abstract: Kirigami is an increasingly useful fabrication method to produce shape-programmable metamaterial structures. However, inverse design remains difficult because deployment is nonlinear, and feasible cut layouts must satisfy discrete compatibility rules, avoid overlap, and map one target shape to valid designs. We present RL-Kirigami, an inverse design framework that combines optimal-transport conditional flow matching (OT-CFM) with reinforcement learning to generate compatible ratio fields for compact reconfigurable parallelogram quad kirigami. A marching decoder enforces global geometric compatibility, and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) aligns the generator with nondifferentiable rewards for silhouette matching, feasibility, and ratio-field regularity. Across procedurally generated target shape instances, a single sample from the pretrained OT-CFM prior reached and outperformed solver baselines while reducing forward simulator evaluations from hundreds to . GRPO improved accuracy to and, with regularity included, reduced from to while maintaining . Generated layouts were exported to DXF and laser cut in polymeric sheets to produce deployable prototypes in minutes per part. These results support a manufacturing-aware inverse design workflow for deployable kirigami metamaterials under geometric feasibility constraints.

title: AI-driven predictive and inverse design framework for defect engineering in hexagonal boron nitride monolayers
abstract: Nanostructured hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) exhibits exceptional mechanical properties; however, its performance is strongly influenced by the unavoidable presence of structural defects. Accurate prediction and targeted engineering of defect-induced properties remain challenging, particularly for complex mixed-defect configurations. In this study, an integrated AI-driven framework is developed for both predictive modeling and inverse design of defective h-BN monolayers. The framework combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for data generation, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for property prediction, and transfer learning to extend predictive capability to mixed-defect systems. Additionally, a data-driven inverse design module is introduced to generate optimal defect configurations with desired mechanical properties. The proposed models achieve mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 13.21 GPa and 3.81 GPa for Young’s modulus and ultimate tensile strength, respectively, with the best-performing transfer learning model demonstrating improved accuracy for mixed-defect configurations. Furthermore, the inverse design module is validated through statistical analysis, showing strong agreement with MD simulation results. Overall, the developed framework provides an efficient surrogate model for accelerated materials design, significantly reducing computational cost while enabling tunable property optimization, with potential applications beyond structural materials.

title: Atomistic insight into short-range order strengthening of TiZrVNb high-entropy alloys
abstract: Chemical short-range order (SRO) critically tailors the mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys (HEAs). However, experimentally characterizing the dynamic evolution of SRO remains challenging, while traditional computations struggle with high costs or limited accuracy. To overcome these barriers, we develop a high-fidelity machine learning potential for the lightweight refractory TiZrVNb HEA using the neuroevolution potential framework, achieving density functional theory (DFT)-level accuracy for large-scale simulations. Using hybrid molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations, we reveal that SRO formation is energetically favored and induces a unique pseudo-composite microstructure. This chemical heterogeneity divides the lattice into body-center-cubic-preferred (BCCP) clusters and hexagonal-close-packed-preferred (HCPP) clusters. Thermodynamically driven by HCPP clusters, localized HCP precursors form spontaneously prior to deformation. While both BCCP and HCPP clusters function as intrinsic hard fillers to enhance strength, the pre-existing HCP precursors maintain ductility by gradually growing during a continuous strain-induced phase transformation. Consequently, the SRO configuration achieves an average increase of approximately 55% in ultimate tensile strength relative to the random state, without compromising ductility. Beyond providing an efficient framework for large-scale simulations of refractory HEAs, this study elucidates the atomic origin of the strength-ductility synergy in TiZrVNb, offering a promising strategy for alloy design via precise SRO manipulation.

title: J-PINN: A domain-decomposed physics-informed neural network framework for kinematic field reconstruction in fracture mechanics
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) solve inverse problems, yet standard formulations fail to resolve the discontinuous fields inherent to fracture mechanics. This study introduces a novel, meshless Multi-Region PINN framework for 2D cracked elastic bodies. By decomposing the domain via strict kinematic constraints, the method restores the validity of the Navier–Cauchy equations within each partition. Validated against FEM, the framework accurately captures stress singularities using sparse boundary data, achieving relative errors below 1% for displacements and 2–4% for strain and stresses. Furthermore, a thermodynamic error-compensation strategy is proposed to correct systematic -integral drift, yielding path-independent strain energy release rate (SERR) estimates. Demonstrating utility for material characterization, the method is applied to experimental Digital Image Correlation (DIC) data from a Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) Double Cantilever Beam. Here, the PINN acts as a physics-informed reconstructor, recovering smooth singular fields from noisy inputs via a robust Huber loss and a physics-driven iterative outlier removal strategy. The calculated SERR ( ) shows strong agreement with analytical Modified Beam Theory (MBT), establishing a robust, assumption-free characterization methodology for interlaminar fracture toughness in fiber-reinforced composites and enabling data-driven extraction of cohesive zone parameters as faithful inputs for composite structural design.

title: Toward autonomous experimentation: Bayesian optimization over problem formulation space for accelerated alloy development
abstract: Accelerated discovery in materials science demands autonomous systems capable of dynamically formulating and solving design problems. In this work, we introduce a novel framework that uses Bayesian optimization over a problem formulation space to identify optimal design formulations in line with decision-maker preferences. By mapping various design scenarios to a multi-attribute utility function, our approach enables the system to balance conflicting objectives—such as ductility, yield strength, density, and solidification range—without requiring an exact problem definition at the outset. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method through an in silico case study on a Mo–Nb–Ti–V–W alloy system targeted for gas turbine engine blade applications. The framework converges on a ‘sweet spot’ that satisfies critical performance thresholds, illustrating that integrating problem formulation discovery into the autonomous design loop can significantly streamline the experimental process. Future work will incorporate human feedback to further enhance the adaptability of the system in real-world experimental settings.

title: Deep learning for the optimal design of phononic crystals in acceleration sensing
abstract: Phononic crystals (PnCs) acceleration sensors have demonstrated strong potential for high-sensitivity sensing due to defect-mode resonance. The acoustic sensitivity of the device is closely related to the topology of the PnCs. However, the large topology design space makes conventional numerical optimization computationally expensive. In this work, we innovatively employ a deep-learning–based framework to identify PnCs structures with optimal acoustic sensitivity. Specifically, an improved convolutional neural network is developed as a surrogate model to predict the performance of PnCs topologies. Based on the surrogate model, a gradient-based optimization strategy is then applied to iteratively refine the PnCs configuration, ultimately yielding the optimal design. The results show that the deep-learning surrogate model achieves an accuracy of 99.12% and a prediction speed approximately times faster than finite-element simulations. Furthermore, the gradient-based optimization yields an acoustic sensitivity of 242.35 kHz/µm after 500 iterations, representing an improvement of about 21.2% compared with conventional cylindrical PnCs. The proposed method enables rapid and accurate identification of the optimal PnCs topology and shows strong potential for broad application across a wide range of metamaterials and microelectromechanical system (MEMS) devices.

title: Z-parameter model based paradigm for fatigue life prediction and quality control
abstract: Manufacturing processes such as welding and additive manufacturing inevitably introduce defects, which pose a significant threat to structural safety. Establishing predictive frameworks that coherently link defect characteristics to fatigue life remains a fundamental challenge in manufacturing science and structural integrity. Existing fatigue models suffer from poor parameter robustness and lack of uncertainty quantification. Here, we establish fatigue life models of materials with different defect features using finite element analysis, and develop a novel hybrid physics-statistical method to achieve robust identification of material-dependent defect sensitivity parameters, improving the reliability of conventional Z -parameter model. Building on this, we propose an original Z -PIHREN framework integrating physics-informed neural networks with heteroscedastic regression and deep ensembles, to quantify fatigue uncertainty and assess structural reliability of defective structures. The model placed 84.2 % of samples within factor-of-three error bounds and achieved a validation-set coverage-calibration R 2 of 0.956 after temperature scaling. More importantly, by establishing quantitative correlations between defects and fatigue life, the proposed framework not only offers forward predictions for reliability assessment of long-term service structures, but also provides inverse guidance for manufacturing process optimization. This work demonstrates the prospect for establishing a physics-statistical framework that integrates fatigue life prediction with quality control in manufacturing.

title: Generative Bayesian machine learning framework for inverse alloy designing of lightweight high entropy alloy with target density and experimental validation
abstract: Lightweight high entropy alloys (LHEAs) are promising next-generation structural materials due to their excellent strength–ductility synergy and thermal stability. However, accurate control of alloy density remains challenging because severe lattice distortion in multicomponent systems often leads to deviations from conventional rule-of-mixture predictions. In this work, a generative Bayesian machine learning framework is developed for the inverse design of LHEAs with targeted density values. Physically informed descriptors based on elemental properties, including atomic weight, valence electron concentration, atomic size mismatch, melting temperature, mixing enthalpy, and electronegativity mismatch, are used to train supervised machine learning models. A Bayesian-optimised extra trees regression model predicts alloy density with high accuracy while providing uncertainty estimates through ensemble variance. A complementary phase classification model ensures physically plausible phase stability. The trained models are integrated into a generative inverse-design workflow to propose candidate LHEA compositions satisfying user-defined density constraints. Selected alloys are synthesised by vacuum arc melting, and experimentally measured densities validate the model predictions. The combined computational-experimental approach demonstrates a practical pathway for uncertainty-aware machine learning-guided discovery and experimental validation of lightweight high entropy alloys to accelerate alloy design.

title: A novel quadratic multilayer heterostructure framework with physics-informed learning for arbitrarily graded rotor disks in high-speed textile spinning
abstract: High-speed textile spinning rotors are subjected to severe centrifugal and thermo-mechanical loads that can induce stress concentrations and interfacial failure. To address these challenges, this study develops a novel multilayer heterostructure quadratic inhomogeneous (MHQI) framework for arbitrarily graded functionally graded material (FGM) rotors. The formulation employs a second-order layerwise representation to capture complex material gradation with minimal discretization. An axisymmetric rotating-disk model is formulated by incorporating material gradation, porosity, thermal effects, and centrifugal loading. The results are validated against finite element analysis, existing multilayer models, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The MHQI model achieves FEA-level accuracy using only two sublayers. Comparable accuracy in conventional multilayer formulations requires eight sublayers, representing a 75% reduction in layerwise discretization. The formulation also eliminates artificial stress discontinuities. For a Ti–ceramic rotor, centrifugal loading dominates the structural response, whereas thermal effects remain secondary. Controlled porosity reduces the effective density and centrifugal stress by up to 25%, while material gradation lowers the radial and hoop stresses by up to 25% and 20%, respectively. The PINN framework further identifies the optimal exponential grading configuration that minimizes the peak hoop stress and accurately recovers unknown gradation parameters from response data. The present framework is limited to steady-state operation at a constant angular velocity and does not consider transient thermo-mechanical effects or rotor dynamic imbalances.

title: Design-oriented multiscale shear behavior of sandstone-concrete interfaces via experiments and physics-informed learning
abstract: Sandstone-concrete interfaces are critical heterogeneous material interfaces in rock-concrete composite structures, where insufficient shear resistance can trigger interfacial instability under low confinement. The key design challenge is to establish a quantitative structure–property link between engineered interface morphology, damage evolution and shear response, while providing a physically consistent prediction tool for untested loading conditions. Here, serrated sandstone-concrete interfaces were examined under normal stress of 0.1–0.8 MPa through 8 direct shear tests combined with acoustic emission, digital image correlation, three-dimensional morphology characterization and ODE-constrained PINN modeling. Peak shear stress increased from 1.49 to 2.94 MPa with normal stress, accompanied by a transition from serration-interlocking brittle fracture to compaction-assisted frictional wear and root shearing. Acoustic-emission and digital-image-correlation results reveal that tensile opening is progressively suppressed and shear-dominated distributed damage develops. Three-dimensional surface metrics further show interface smoothing, with S a and S q decreasing by 20.8 % and 23.5 %, respectively. The proposed model, trained only on 0.1–0.6 MPa curves, predicted unseen 0.7–0.8 MPa responses with 9.17 % normalized root-mean-square error and peak errors below 2 %. This work provides design-relevant guidance for tailoring sandstone-concrete interface morphology and a physics-constrained framework for predicting shear resistance.

title: Directional acoustic meta-sensor with gradient impedance matching meta-material
abstract: We propose a gradient-impedance directional sensing metamaterial achieving simultaneous high sound pressure gain and precision. Featuring a 5-stage concentric arc cascade channel with continuously varying cross-sections, it forms a 4-channel orthogonal array to calculate incident sound direction via the orthogonal difference method. This gradient cross-section acts as a broadband impedance transformer, enhancing the linear physical gain by 66.0% compared to conventional designs. It excites efficient localized Mie resonances within 300–1500 Hz, achieving a peak sound pressure gain of 13.7 times (22.7 dB) and an average gain of 4.7 times (13.4 dB).To decouple phase interference perturbations from third-order spatial harmonics, we introduce an analytical multipole expansion-based error compensation algorithm. This improves 360° omnidirectional tracking accuracy by 17.2%. Absolute positioning residuals are restricted within a ± 5.0° confidence interval, yielding a final prediction accuracy of 89.3%. This hardware-algorithm synergistic approach inspires compact, high-fidelity acoustic positioning terminals in complex soundscapes.

title: Benchmarking and assessing models of reactor pressure vessel steel embrittlement
abstract: Accurate prediction of ductile-to-brittle transition temperature shifts (TTS) of steel alloys used in reactor pressure vessels (RPVs) is critical for informing safe and reliable nuclear reactor operation. Recently, numerous physically-motivated semiempirical and data-driven machine learning (ML) models of TTS for RPVs have been developed. Here, we present detailed benchmarks of the most widely used models and discuss their pros and cons based on statistical metrics on key data subsets (e.g., predicting TTS of steels under reactor life extension conditions of low flux and high fluence) and their physical trends with key variables (e.g., irradiation flux and fluence). In addition, we develop an ensemble neural network ML model that includes a physics-informed loss function component which penalizes unphysical changes in TTS with flux and fluence. We show that this model overcomes shortcomings in a similar earlier model related to extrapolation to higher fluence over a range of flux values from low flux life extension conditions up to high flux test reactor conditions. We show detailed per-alloy and highest fluence data predictions, and provide life extension predictions for the US nuclear reactor alloys. Finally, we have developed a codebase to make the use and evaluation of all models readily accessible to the broader community. It is our hope this codebase can grow to encompass new models developed by the community and function as an informative benchmark for modeling of RPV steel embrittlement in the future.

title: Application of cerium oxide nanoparticle for root canal disinfection
abstract: This study evaluated cerium oxide nanoparticles (CNPs) as adjunctive disinfectants for refractory Enterococcus faecalis ( E. faecalis ) root canal infections. CNPs were characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Cytocompatibility with MC3T3-E1 cells and human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs) was assessed using fluorescence staining and flow cytometry. The antibacterial activity of CNPs against E. faecalis and its biofilms was evaluated using colony-forming unit (CFU) counting, SEM, confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM), flow cytometry, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) detection. CNPs induced sustained ROS generation, oxidative stress, and bacterial membrane disruption. In an ex vivo refractory root canal infection model, CNPs combined with conventional irrigants (NaOCl/EDTA) and passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI) enhanced root canal disinfection and dentinal tubule cleaning. Moreover, when used as intracanal medicaments, CNPs promoted bacterial killing and deep intratubular penetration. A one-dimensional hindered diffusion model further simulated the spatiotemporal transport of CNPs within dentinal tubules. These findings suggest that biocompatible CNPs may serve as a promising adjunctive strategy for managing refractory root canal infections through ROS-mediated antibacterial activity and intratubular transport.

title: Physics-informed FEA–GPR–PSO optimization of perforated CARALL structures for simultaneous bending strength increase and lightweight design
abstract: Fiber metal laminates combine the advantages of metals and carbon fiber–reinforced polymers, among which carbon fiber–reinforced aluminum laminates (CARALLs) have attracted significant attention due to their excellent mechanical performance. However, insufficient bonding strength at the metal–adhesive interface often leads to interfacial delamination. Perforating the metal layer to form pin-like mechanical interlocking structures is an effective solution, while also enabling weight reduction. Nevertheless, perforation design involves multiple geometric parameters, including hole diameter, pitch-to-diameter ratio, hole type, and staggered arrangement, and improper combinations may induce stress concentration and stiffness degradation. Moreover, systematic optimization strategies suitable for high-end industrial applications remain limited. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-guided, data-driven optimization framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), Gaussian process regression (GPR), and particle swarm optimization (PSO) for perforated CFRP–aluminum–CFRP laminates. Experimental tests were conducted to calibrate and validate the FEA model. Based on an experimental design, surrogate models were established for tensile and bending strength, achieving normalized root mean squared errors of 4.14 % and 3.35 %, respectively. Global optimization results demonstrate a 5.47 % reduction in structural weight and a 9.52 % improvement in bending strength, with only a 1.82 % decrease in tensile strength, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed framework in balancing design.

title: Towards generalizable thermal profile prediction in additive manufacturing using constrained random walks and machine learning
abstract: Defect formation in additively manufactured materials is strongly governed by the thermal history experienced during printing, which depends on process parameters that interact in complex and often non-linear ways. A finite element method (FEM) model was developed to extract thermal profiles at representative locations in laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) processes, iterating over a defined set of printing parameters under a single scanning strategy. Among the machine learning architectures evaluated, Neural Networks (NN) provided the most accurate and robust predictions. To generalise the approach beyond fixed scanning strategies, a constrained random walks (CRW) methodology has been introduced to generate training datasets with sufficient variability. The resulting model predicts thermal histories accurately and at a fraction of the computational cost of FEM, providing a practical basis for process optimisation and defect control in L-PBF.

title: Smart response food-derived polysaccharide hydrogels: reprogramming the microenvironment for skin rejuvenation
abstract: Skin aging is a multifaceted biological process marked by the disruption of the ROS-MMP-collagen axis, resulting in the degradation of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and compromised barrier function. Traditional synthetic interventions often face challenges related to biocompatibility and limited efficacy in targeted delivery. In contrast, food-derived polysaccharide hydrogels (FDPH) have emerged as a novel class of bio-instructive materials. These hydrogels extend beyond the conventional role of passive scaffolds by leveraging their intrinsic bioactivity and tunable three-dimensional architectures, which may contribute to the modulation of aging-associated microenvironmental factors. This review offers a comprehensive critical analysis of the evolution of FDPH from their initial role as structural fillers to their current status as sophisticated therapeutic platforms. These platforms are capable of detecting pathological signals, including pH, ROS, and enzymes, thus facilitating more precise and localized therapeutic interventions.We explore the molecular mechanisms that underpin their dual functionality in mitigating oxidative stress and influencing fibroblast-associated regenerative processes that may support collagen remodeling. Additionally, it identifies challenges such as structural variability, transdermal efficiency, and long-term safety. The review also predicts future trends in precision design and personalized applications, fueled by AI and multi-omics, guiding the advancement of FDPH for skin health and anti-aging.

title: Impurity concentration prediction of Czochralski silicon based on domain-adversarial transfer learning: Physical consistency and cross-furnace adaptability study
abstract: This study presents a domain-adversarial transfer learning (DATL) framework for the precise prediction and control of impurity concentrations in Czochralski silicon, directly addressing the persistent challenges of data scarcity, poor model transferability, and limited robustness in industrial deployment. By integrating simulation and industrial data through adversarial learning, DATL distills domain-invariant physical laws, thereby suppressing negative transfer and ensuring physical consistency. In oxygen content prediction, DATL demonstrates high accuracy (RMSE = 1.099 ppma) with 1147 samples and robust resistance to process noise and drift. Its key advantage is data-efficient commissioning of a new furnace, achieving high accuracy (RMSE = 1.307 ppma) with only 302 samples. Ablation studies identify the domain-adversarial mechanism as the direct source of this adaptability and robustness. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis not only identifies and ranks the governing physical parameters, but also, by analyzing parameter-specific contributions across six industrial scenarios, directly yields a hierarchical control strategy. This effectively bridges interpretable prediction with actionable process control. This work delivers a practical solution for rapid furnace qualification and stabilized yield. More broadly, it establishes a paradigm of distilling domain-invariant physics via adversarial learning, paving the way for managing diverse impurities and advancing adaptive intelligent manufacturing in crystal growth.

title: Machine learning-mediated composition-process optimization and high strength-toughness performance achievement of ductile iron
abstract: To overcome the high cost and inefficiency associated with traditional trial-and-error methods in optimizing the strength and toughness of ductile cast iron, this study proposes an intelligent design framework that combines physical metallurgy features with machine learning. By combining composition-process data with atomic-scale elemental attributes, a high-dimensional feature space was constructed. Multi-level feature screening was employed to extract key interactive features influencing ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elongation (EL). High-precision performance prediction models were developed based on a multilayer perceptron, and inverse design of three composition-process schemes for ductile cast iron with balanced high strength and high toughness was achieved by integrating the NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm. Experimental validation confirmed their excellent mechanical properties, the UTS reaches 940 MPa, and the EL reaches 6.3%. SHAP analysis further elucidated the regulatory mechanisms of the key features. As a preliminary exploratory extension, the proposed feature engineering method was preliminarily applied to a 7xxx series aluminum alloy in the T6 temper. The model achieved promising predictive performance, with an R 2 of 0.90 for UTS and 0.87 for EL. These results preliminarily suggest that this feature construction strategy may have the potential to be transferred to other precipitation-hardened alloy systems.

title: Generative inverse design of cold metals for low-power electronics
abstract: Cold metals possess an intrinsic energy gap located close to the Fermi level, which enables cold-carrier injection for steep-slope transistors and is therefore promising for low-power electronics. High-throughput screening has revealed 252 three-dimensional (3D) cold metals in the Materials Project database, but database searches are inherently limited to known compounds. Here we present an inverse-design workflow that generates 3D cold metals using MatterGPT, a conditional autoregressive Transformer trained on SLICES, an invertible and symmetry-invariant crystal representation. We curate a training set of 26,309 metallic structures labeled with energy above hull and a unified band-edge distance descriptor that merges p-type and n-type features to address severe label imbalance. Property-conditioned generation targeting thermodynamic stability and 50–500 meV band-edge distances produces 148,506 unique candidates; 92.1 % are reconstructed into 3D structures and down-selected by symmetry, uniqueness and novelty filters, followed by high-throughput DFT validation. We identify 257 cold metals absent from the Materials Project database, all within the targeted 50–500 meV window. First-principles phonon, electronic-structure, and work-function calculations for representative candidates confirm dynamical stability and contact-relevant work functions. Our results demonstrate that SLICES-enabled generative transformers can expand the chemical space of cold metals beyond high-throughput screening, providing a route to low-power electronic materials discovery.

title: Feasibility-guided inverse design of pressure-tunable interlocking structures using random forest
abstract: Structures with tunable mechanical properties enable adaptive load bearing and energy absorption, yet their inverse design remains challenging because structural parameters, confinement conditions, and mechanical responses are coupled through nonlinear and many-to-one relationships. These difficulties are amplified in small-data settings, where deep generative models are hard to train and often lack physical interpretability. Here, we propose a random-forest-guided inverse-design framework for tunable-stiffness interlocking structures under prescribed confinement conditions. A calibrated RF forward model identifies feasible design regions for a target stiffness band and generates diverse candidate structures through likelihood-guided sampling, avoiding direct learning of a nonunique response-to-design mapping. Using fewer than 250 finite-element-generated geometry–pressure samples, the framework demonstrates improved sample efficiency, feasible-design ranking, and design-space coverage compared with genetic algorithms and covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategies. PDP, SHAP, and interaction analyses reveal how pressure and geometry jointly control stiffness accessibility and regime transitions. Additional finite element analyses show that increasing confinement activates inter-particle contacts, promotes particle rearrangement, enhances frictional dissipation, and forms connected force-transmission pathways, thereby increasing stiffness, peak force, and energy absorption. The calcaneal off-loading example further demonstrates the framework’s potential for application-oriented design of adaptive load-bearing and energy-absorbing systems.

title: Regression-based explainable deep learning for estimating Hamiltonian parameters from magnetic nanodot images
abstract: Magnetic nanodots host topological spin textures whose stability is dictated by an extended Heisenberg Hamiltonian combining symmetric exchange, the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, magnetocrystalline anisotropy, and the Zeeman field. Inferring these atomistic parameters from two-dimensional magnetization images underpins the design of functional magnetic materials, yet it remains an ill-posed inverse problem: under certain external conditions and transient states, configurations relax into noisy, weakly discriminative textures that render the dataset ill-conditioned. Deep-learning estimators act as opaque black boxes and rely on slow atomistic simulations. We propose an explainable regression methodology whose novelty lies in data generation and interpretability: a matrix decomposition of the extended Hamiltonian enables GPU-accelerated Metropolis–Hastings Monte Carlo with simulated annealing, accelerating computation without altering the underlying physics, while Regression Activation Maps (RAMs), a novel error-based attribution metric, turn the network into a traceable gray-box model. Trained on several configurations, convolutional and Vision Transformer regressors reliably recover the physical parameters from simulated nanodot images, while the higher-order exchange constants remain bounded by the intrinsic identifiability limits of the s z projection. Comparing both families through their attention maps and accuracy-versus-size trade-off, RAMs isolate the chiral domain walls and skyrmion cores driving predictions.

title: Data-driven inverse design of a dual-stiffness TPMS fusion cage with experimental validation
abstract: Data-driven design of architected biomedical structures requires controllable geometry-property relationships and experimental validation of manufacturable designs. This study proposed an inverse design framework for a dual-stiffness triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) fusion cage by integrating parametric finite element analysis (FEA), deep learning, laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), and mechanical testing. A TPMS-Gyroid cage was parameterized by wall thickness, internal gap, pillar dimension, and unit-cell size to regulate contact-induced stiffness transition. FEA identified parameter effects on staged stiffness, transition load, and porosity. Based on 800 simulated designs, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) was trained to establish the nonlinear geometry-property mapping, achieving high predictive accuracy ( ) for force, elastic modulus, cage height, and porosity, and enabling inverse generation of geometric parameters from target mechanical performance. Optimized Ti6Al4 V cages were fabricated by LPBF and evaluated under uniaxial compression, three-point bending, and eccentric loading, representing flexion, extension, and bending, respectively. The experimental results agreed well with the numerical predictions and confirmed a robust bilinear, contact-induced dual-stiffness response. The cages showed a compliant first stage, second stage modulus of to , and porosity of to . This work provides a complete, transferable data-driven design route for additively manufactured TPMS fusion cages.

title: Wide-range predictions of hydrogen-dependent vacancy diffusion in nickel from a near-DFT-accurate machine-learning potential
abstract: Vacancy-mediated atomic transport plays a central role in high-temperature creep and microstructural evolution. Pure Ni provides a representative model system because Ni is the principal matrix element of many Ni-based heat-resistant alloys, while its prototypical FCC structure enables the intrinsic effects of hydrogen to be isolated. However, quantitative understanding of how hydrogen modifies vacancy formation, migration, and the resulting self-diffusion in Ni over wide temperature and pressure ranges remains limited. We therefore develop a near-DFT-accurate machine-learning moment tensor potential for the Ni–vacancy–hydrogen system and map the vacancy diffusion coefficient over 300 – 1500 K and hydrogen gas pressures – . The equilibrium vacancy concentration is obtained from the vacancy formation free-energy, while the hydrogen-dependent jump frequency is evaluated from the activation free-energy using the excess hydrogen thermodynamic integration method. The maps show that hydrogen suppresses vacancy diffusion at low temperatures over the entire investigated range of , whereas it enhances vacancy diffusion at high temperatures. Incorporating the hydrogen-enhanced equilibrium vacancy concentration, the vacancy-mediated Ni self-diffusivity increases under hydrogen charging for all conditions, with the strongest acceleration at low temperature and high H 2 pressure.

title: Nanoconjugated caffeic acid-gold nanoparticles for passive diffusion of simulated blood-brain barrier and neuroprotective activity
