abstract: Efficient transport of antioxidant therapeutics across brain-associated barriers remains a major challenge for neuroprotective strategies. Here, we report caffeic acid–functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs–CA) engineered to enhance passive diffusion and provide intrinsic redox activity. Monodisperse ∼ 12 nm AuNPs were synthesized and covalently conjugated with caffeic acid, yielding stable nanoconjugated systems that retained the catechol–quinone redox interconversion essential for antioxidant function. Transport properties were evaluated using a non-cellular, electrospun PMMA–gelatin scaffold designed as a simplified passive-diffusion model that mimics selected structural features of the blood–brain barrier. AuNPs–CA exhibited controlled release of caffeic acid under enzymatic degradation and demonstrated significantly improved diffusion compared to free CA. SH-SY5Y neuronal-like cells showed high viability upon exposure to the nanoconjugated systems and also preserved their normal morphology. Antioxidant assays confirmed strong radical-scavenging activity, indicating that the conjugation strategy maintains the redox functionality of caffeic acid. These findings establish AuNPs–CA as a dual-function nanoplatform that couples enhanced passive diffusion through a simulated barrier with robust neuroprotective properties, supporting their potential utility in future therapeutic approaches targeting oxidative stress–related neurodegenerative conditions.

title: Adaptive horizons in 4D printing: stimuli-responsive materials, computational intelligence, biomedical translation, and sustainable futures
abstract: Four-dimensional (4D) printing has emerged as a transformative paradigm in additive manufacturing that uniquely incorporates time as the fourth dimension, extending static three-dimensional constructs into dynamic, stimuli-responsive architectures capable of programmed evolution over time. Unlike conventional 3D printing, which produces static geometries, 4D printing creates adaptive structures with programmability, temporal functionality, and reconfigurability that enable active interaction with their environment.This review critically synthesizes advances across seven interconnected domains: theoretical foundations, material innovations, fabrication modalities, biomedical translation, computational intelligence, reproducibility and ethical accountability, and sustainability with future directions. Stimuli-responsive materials, including shape memory polymers, liquid crystal elastomers, hydrogels, ceramics, metals, and cell-laden biomaterials, provide diverse actuation pathways, while fabrication strategies such as digital light processing, two-photon polymerization, direct ink writing, extrusion-based printing, and bioprinting translate these capabilities into functional constructs. Biomedical applications demonstrate translational potential, achieving > 90% cell viability and vascularization within seven days across tissue engineering, implantable devices, and drug delivery platforms. Recent advances in 4D-printed cardiac occluders, vascular stents, intestinal stents, and patient-specific surgical guides further underscore the clinical relevance of this technology. Computational intelligence accelerates design cycles via machine learning, topology optimization, and multi-physics simulations, achieving prediction accuracies above 90% and design cycle reductions exceeding 50%. Reliability and reproducibility frameworks safeguard scientific integrity, while ethical considerations, including informed consent, data privacy, and equitable access, ensure responsible biomedical translation. Sustainability is advanced through recyclable resins, eco-friendly energy devices, and bioinspired composites, while emerging cell contractile force-mediated actuation opens new frontiers in biologically driven morphogenesis. Despite these achievements, critical challenges persist in scalability, high-throughput biofabrication, and standardized evaluation frameworks-gaps that this review systematically addresses. By integrating adaptive materials, computational design, and ethical accountability, 4D printing redefines the boundaries of manufacturing and sets the stage for next-generation technological innovation in personalized medicine, sustainable infrastructure, and intelligent functional devices.

title: Hydrogel particles under uniaxial compression: Tetrapod-based DEM approach and experimental validation
abstract: Hydrogels are soft, water-rich polymer networks whose mechanical behavior governs applications from biomedicine to packed bed processes. In aerogel manufacturing, hydrogel particles represent an intermediate state in which mechanical stability determines scalability and process reliability. However, predictive particle-scale models for deformable matrix-fluid systems remain limited. Biopolymer-based hydrogel particles are investigated under uniaxial compression through monotonic, cyclic, and stress-relaxation experiments at compression rates of 0.1-3.0 mm/s. Apparent stiffness increased strongly with rate, followed by saturation above 0.5 mm/s, where the apparent Young’s modulus became rate independent. Within the elastic regime, the response is reproducible and hysteretic, whereas higher strains induced plastic deformation. Aging over one year led to additional stiffening, indicating ongoing structural evolution. To complement the experiments, a novel discrete-element-method framework based on tetrapod-shaped parcels is introduced. Tetrapods qualitatively represent the 3D polymer network and predominantly carry mechanical loads, while embedded spheres mimic the aqueous phase. Parameters are calibrated using a full-factorial design and Bayesian optimization. Simulations reproduce the force–strain response, apparent elastic properties, and particle deformation. Random packings produce comparable scatter, while stress relaxation and cyclic loading are reproduced qualitatively. The approach advances predictive modeling of deformable particles and provides a basis for solvent exchange and process-scale simulations.

title: Uncertainty-aware structure–property mapping of spinodoid metamaterials via heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression
abstract: Spinodoid metamaterials provide a tunable design space for anisotropic mechanical properties, but their structure–property relationships are commonly represented as deterministic mappings from cone-angle descriptors to single stiffness values. This view overlooks the stochastic nature of Gaussian random field (GRF)-based topology generation, in which identical descriptors produce different morphologies and property scatter. We present an uncertainty-aware framework that interprets cone-angle descriptors as defining input-dependent stiffness distributions. Using heteroscedastic Gaussian process regression (GPR), the framework infers a low-dimensional, globally shared noise function from residual patterns across sparse observations. The results show that morphology-induced scatter varies across the design space and among stiffness components according to their mechanically active directions. Designs with similar mean stiffness can therefore exhibit different aleatoric uncertainty. In reliability-based design optimization (RBDO), direct repeated-realization validation confirms that only the heteroscedastic RBDO design satisfies the prescribed reliability target, whereas deterministic optimization and homoscedastic RBDO remain vulnerable to constraint violations. Accounting for heteroscedasticity therefore improves design reliability by incorporating spatial variation in morphology-induced scatter. These findings establish an uncertainty-aware framework for spinodoid modeling and design, while nonlinear responses and correlation-aware multi-output surrogates remain for future work.

title: Interpretable machine learning-assisted inverse design of high-strength and ductile cast magnesium alloys
abstract: Cast rare-earth (RE) magnesium (Mg) alloys are governed by strong coupling among multicomponent compositions, elemental interactions, and heat treatment parameters, making on-demand design difficult using trial-and-error methods or conventional ML models with limited interpretability. Here, an interpretable ML-assisted composition-processing inverse design strategy was developed from a dataset of 1367 cast RE Mg alloy records. Model screening identified LightGBM for tensile yield strength (TYS) prediction and XGBoost for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and elongation (EL). After hyperparameter optimization and stacking integration, the final models achieved test-set R 2 values of 0.92, 0.92, and 0.84 for TYS, UTS, and EL, respectively. SHAP and PDP analyses revealed the effects of key compositions, elemental interaction features, and heat treatment parameters, which were coupled with NSGA-II-based multi-objective inverse optimization. Pareto-front screening yielded 139 candidates, and two representative alloys were experimentally validated. After T6 treatment, strength-oriented Alloy1 reached 294 MPa TYS, 336 MPa UTS, and 11.2% EL, while ductility- oriented Alloy2 achieved 207 MPa, 301 MPa, and 21.4%, respectively, with all prediction errors below 10.5%. These results demonstrate interpretable ML-enabled on-demand design of cast RE Mg alloys with targeted strength or ductility.

title: Symmetry-aware framework for bidirectional modeling of 3D photonic crystals and band structures
abstract: The precise calculation of photonic band structures and the inverse design of unit cell structures based on spectral targets are pivotal tasks in 3D photonic crystal researches. However, data-driven approaches in this domain are severely constrained by the scarcity of high-fidelity volumetric data due to the prohibitive computational costs of 3D simulations. To address this bottleneck, we leverage the high-throughput capabilities of the FAME package Lyu et al. (2021) [1] to construct a comprehensive benchmark database comprising tens of thousands of cubic photonic crystals. Building upon this data foundation, we propose a deep learning framework for the bidirectional modeling of 3D PhCs. This architecture synergizes a symmetry-aware attention mechanism for precise forward prediction with a conditional denoising diffusion implicit model for inverse design. This “generate-evaluate-select” closed-loop strategy resolves the intrinsic ill-posedness of inverse scattering, enabling the probabilistic exploration of geometrically diverse candidate structures with similar surrogate-predicted spectra. We demonstrate the framework’s versatility by engineering robust, geometrically regular, connectivity-screened structures for targeted band flattening and candidate local slow-light behavior. By explicitly accounting for geometric regularity, our work provides a viable computational strategy for discovering functional 3D optical metamaterials that balance spectral fidelity with geometric regularity and connectivity screening; quantitative process-level manufacturability assessment is left to future work.

title: Data-efficient Bayesian-guided design selection from large candidate sets: Application to hyperelastic stochastic metamaterials
abstract: From a pool of admissible designs, we aim to identify a structure that achieves a target macroscopic stress response. For each candidate, the response is obtained from a high-fidelity oracle, such as expensive computational homogenization or experiments. We consider cases in which (i) the geometry cannot be conveniently parameterized, rendering gradient-based optimization inapplicable, and (ii) brute-force evaluation of all candidates is infeasible due to costly oracle queries. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Bayesian-guided design selection framework. The dimensionality of design variants is reduced through statistical feature engineering, and the resulting low-dimensional descriptors are mapped to effective hyperelastic constitutive parameters using a multi-output Gaussian process surrogate. The surrogate is trained using uncertainty-driven active learning with only a limited number of high-fidelity oracle evaluations. The surrogate shortlists promising candidates, and since its accuracy is inherently limited, the final selection of the optimal design is performed through high-fidelity oracle evaluations within the shortlist. In numerical test cases, we consider a design set of 50,000 candidate structures. Active learning requires labeling less than half a percent of the entire candidate set. Bayesian-guided design selection reaches a prescribed error threshold with only a handful of oracle evaluations in most cases.

title: Defect engineering of semiconductor photocatalysts for solar energy conversion: from atomic-level design to AI-driven materials discovery for sustainable development and clean energy
abstract: The solar energy conversion based on semiconductor photocatalysis suffers from the low absorption of visible light, the quick recombination of charge carriers, the slow surface reaction kinetics and the low long-term stability. Although defect engineering has become an exciting approach to address these challenges, the link between the design of defects at the atomic level, computational modelling, and the use of AI to discover materials has yet to be fully established. It critically examines the intrinsic and extrinsic defects including vacancies, interstitials, substitutional dopants, antisite defects, grain boundaries and dislocations, and their effects on the electronic structure, charge separation, surface reaction pathways, stability and scalability of representative semiconductor photocatalysts. The oxygen-vacancy engineering always delivers excellent photocatalytic efficiency, with the heteroatom doping and interface modulation, from the comparative analysis. This review also brings together recent developments in operando characterization, DFT, molecular dynamics, high throughput screening, machine learning, digital twins, and AI-assisted inverse design for predictive development of catalysts for clean energy. Finally, important challenges related to stability of defects, reproducible synthesis, techno-economic feasibility and commercialization are identified providing a roadmap for the development of scalable, intelligent and high-performance photocatalysts for hydrogen evolution, CO 2 reduction and nitrogen fixation.

title: Inverse design of lightweight manufacturable TPMS structures based on a constitutive-aware neural operator
abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures have conventionally relied on inefficient trial-and-error forward design. Existing data-driven inverse approaches, dominated by generative adversarial networks (GANs) and more recently diffusion models, suffer from core drawbacks: training instability, poor physical consistency, neglect of additive manufacturing constraints, and a fixed relative density. Here, we propose a fabrication-aware deterministic inverse design framework driven by a Constitutive-Aware Neural Operator (CANO). This framework achieves end-to-end integration of the neural operator with differentiable manufacturing constraints, unlocks the joint optimization of topology and density, and realizes the efficient inversion from target mechanical properties to manufacturable geometric parameters of lightweight TPMS structures. Our framework encodes all smooth TPMS topological variants through a four-parameter continuous implicit function, treats relative density ρ ∈ [0.05, 0.20] as an independent design variable, and constructs a four-dimensional continuously differentiable design space. We train a manufacturability proxy network (MPN) and embed its logarithmic barrier term into the optimization objective, thereby realizing fully differentiable integration of additive manufacturing geometric constraints and eliminating post-hoc geometric screening. The forward prediction model attains coefficients of determination (R 2 ) of 0.940 for compressive strength and 0.982 for elastic modulus. At identical relative density and unit cell size, the inversely designed customized topologies deliver 14.9 % higher strength and 34.7 % higher modulus than the classic Gyroid, and 34.9 % and 81.1 % improvements over the Primitive, respectively. Measured mechanical responses closely match the design targets. The mean experimental relative errors are 4.1 % for compressive strength and 9.9 % for elastic modulus, with corresponding 95 % t-confidence intervals of −2.6 % to 10.8 % and 7.8 % to 12.1 %. This work provides a verifiable engineering framework for performance-driven customization of carbon-fiber-reinforced composite TPMS structures.

title: Metamorphic green nanomaterials: bio-responsive architectures for adaptive theranostics
abstract: Adaptive nanomaterials are emerging as a cornerstone of sustainable theranostics, offering intelligent, responsive, and environmentally responsible solutions to complex biomedical challenges. This perspective introduces metamorphic green nanomaterials as a paradigm shift from static constructs to dynamic bio-responsive systems. Traditionally, green nanomaterials have been valued for eco-friendly synthesis and passive biocompatibility. In this work, we explore how they can be re-engineered to undergo pre-programmed architectural and functional transformations in situ upon encountering specific biological cues. Such metamorphosis, through controlled disassembly, reassembly, or shape-shifting, unlocks emergent functionalities at target sites, enabling adaptive theranostic capabilities. We discuss how converging innovations in the biosynthesis of complex precursors, dynamic DNA/RNA nanotechnology, biocatalytic triggers, and AI-driven computational co-design are pivotal to realizing these multi-state systems. Potential applications include sequential drug delivery cascades that overcome biological barriers and resistance, sense-and-remediate platforms for pathogenic niches or environmental pollutants, and dynamic scaffolds for regenerative medicine that adapt to evolving tissue needs. While challenges remain in fidelity and scalable manufacturing, the inherent biocompatibility and sustainability of green components provide unique advantages. Metamorphic green nanomaterials may represent a step toward autonomous living nanomachines and may advance theranostic technologies through enhanced intelligence, adaptability, and ecological responsibility, paving the way for personalized nanomedicine.

title: Bridging data gaps in polymer additive manufacturing via knowledge-informed, LLM intelligence guided prompt engineering for 3D-printed PLA tensile-strength prediction
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has shown potential to transform additive manufacturing (AM). However, the lack of sufficient training data is a challenge. This paper presents a knowledge-informed prompt-engineering approach that utilizes large language models (LLMs) to generate physically meaningful synthetic data related to 3D-printed polylactic acid (PLA). The objective is to answer two important questions: (a) whether LLMs can generate synthetic data to improve AM machine learning models? If yes, (b) what type of prompting approaches can be most beneficial? Using a mixed experimental dataset collected across two laboratories, we design seven structured prompting strategies to generate synthetic datasets, integrate them with experimental data, followed by evaluation across five conventional classification ML models and a multilayer perceptron (MLP). Our studies reveal that small injections of synthetic data, such as 10%−20% (or 5–10 points) of the number of real data, generally lead to stable ML model performance, whereas large injections such as 200% or more generally degrade the accuracy. Among the models, XGBoost and CatBoost demonstrate the strongest performance. The numeric, few-shot prompts result in the highest average macro-F1 score of ∼0.92. Our results indicate that LLM-driven, prompt-engineered synthetic data generation can serve as effective approach for overcoming AM data scarcity.

title: Data-augmented crystal graph convolutional neural network for uncertainty-aware thermodynamic stability prediction of two-dimensional MXene/MoS2 materials
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) MXenes and molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) are promising functional materials, but density functional theory (DFT) evaluation of thermodynamic stability is computationally expensive. This study develops a crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) framework to predict formation energy ( E f ) and energy above the convex hull ( E hull ) from a limited dataset of 414 Materials Project structures. The limited dataset represents epistemic uncertainty, while controlled atom-wise perturbations represent local structural variability, whereas rigid translation is used as an invariance control. CGCNN hyperparameters were selected using an L 9 (3 4 ) orthogonal array with analysis of means and range analysis. Among the evaluated augmentation strategies, the combined shift case achieved the lowest mean absolute errors of 0.0052 and 0.0058 eV atom −1 for E f and E hull , respectively. Separately, the three repeated baseline models were used to construct validation-calibrated 95% prediction intervals for uncertainty-aware screening of held-out structures, with 97.6% empirical coverage for both targets. The results demonstrate a practical small-data workflow for thermodynamic stability prediction while highlighting reduced reliability in sparsely represented unstable regions.

title: Machine learning-driven multi-objective optimisation of shape-memory programming parameters in 4D-printed PLA
abstract: 4D printing extends additive manufacturing by introducing time-dependent functionality through stimuli-responsive feedstocks such as shape-memory polymers (SMPs). In 4D-printed PLA, performance is governed by programming temperature, holding time, and recovery temperature, whose effects are reflected in recovery time, shape fixity ratio, and shape recovery ratio. This study combines a replicated 49-condition Latin-square design, machine-learning surrogate models, NSGA-II multi-objective optimisation, and experimental validation to identify a Pareto-optimal process window. Eight regression models were evaluated using leave-one-condition-out (LOCO) cross-validation with nested hyperparameter selection. The surrogates achieved LOCO R 2 values of 0.973 (RMSE 7.29 s) for recovery time, 0.874 (1.17 percentage points, pp) for the shape fixity ratio, and 0.975 (4.31 pp) for the shape recovery ratio. The shape fixity ratio increased from 90.2% to 98.8% between 50 and 55 °C before plateauing, with no significant additional effect of holding time. NSGA-II identified a knee point at 67.5 °C programming temperature, 2.0 min holding time, and 80.0 °C recovery temperature, predicting a recovery time of 3.14 s, shape fixity ratio of 99.72%, and shape recovery ratio of 91.70%. Across five validation points, maximum absolute deviations were 0.36 s, 0.75 pp, and 3.82 pp for recovery time, shape fixity ratio, and shape recovery ratio

title: Leveraging machine learning to predict oxidation kinetics in interconnect alloys for solid oxide cell applications
abstract: In energy conversion technologies, solid oxide cells (SOCs) play a vital role, operating as both fuel and electrolysis cells. In SOC stacks, metallic interconnects are crucial, as they enable electrical connectivity, oxidant/fuel gas distribution, and structural stability. Oxidation during service is a significant challenge, compromising the long-term durability of interconnect alloys. Machine learning (ML) models are employed to predict the oxidation kinetics of SOC interconnects, addressing the complex interactions between alloy design and operating conditions. A comprehensive dataset is gathered from the literature, incorporating key inputs including alloy chemistry, service temperature, and atmosphere composition. The natural logarithm of the parabolic oxidation rate constant, ln( k p ), is regarded as the prediction target. Seven models are developed and tuned, achieving R 2 values of 0.90–0.95. Experimental oxidation data from SS441 interconnects, oxidized in air at 750–850 °C for up to 1500 h, are used as unseen validation data to confirm the predictive capability of the models. The integration of a data-driven approach with oxidation kinetics analysis provides deeper insight into the interplay between alloy design, service conditions, and oxidation behavior. The results demonstrate ML as a powerful tool for optimizing interconnect materials in SOC applications.

title: Unidirectional Cu filling of TGVs using highly-concentrated Cu-MSA electrolytes
abstract: Glass substrates have recently attracted considerable attention as next-generation semiconductor packaging platforms capable of replacing conventional Si interposers and organic substrates for AI accelerators and other advanced semiconductor packages. However, the commercialization of glass substrates is hindered by their low manufacturing yield and poor process productivity. Through-glass vias (TGVs) provide the essential vertical electrical interconnections in glass substrates and are typically formed by Cu electrodeposition. Among the representative TGV filling strategies, unidirectional filling effectively suppresses void formation but suffers from long filling times due to severe mass transport limitations. In this study, highly concentrated Cu-methanesulfonic acid (Cu-MSA) electrolytes were developed to achieve higher Cu ion concentrations than conventional Cu-H 2 SO 4 electrolytes and thereby accelerate unidirectional TGV filling. The physicochemical and electrochemical properties of the Cu-MSA electrolytes were systematically characterized, and a rapid screening method based on short-time electrode potential monitoring was established to determine the maximum operating current density of each electrolyte. Consequently, highly concentrated Cu-MSA electrolytes enabled defect-free unidirectional TGV filling with a 2.30-fold increase in process productivity compared with the conventional H 2 SO 4 -based electrolyte. These findings provide an effective strategy for improving the productivity of unidirectional TGV metallization.

title: A machine learning-mediated composition-microstructure-property multiscale mapping approach for the design of high-strength and high-toughness ductile cast iron
abstract: To overcome the strength–plasticity trade–off and the inefficiency of trial–and–error in ductile cast iron, we develop a machine–learning framework for inverse design from mechanical properties to composition via multiscale mapping. Using 336 experimental datasets with KNN imputation and outlier removal, we construct forward GBRT/RF models linking composition, microstructure, and properties, with SHAP analysis quantifying elemental effects. A two–stage inverse model (GBRT + RF) and Pareto optimization enable property–driven microstructure and composition design. Three designed alloys are experimentally validated. For the three experimentally validated designs, the absolute prediction errors are within 30 MPa for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and 0.5 % for elongation (EL), while the relative prediction errors are within 3 % and 9 %, respectively. Notably, Design 3 achieves UTS of 970 MPa and EL of 5.1 %—over 120 MPa higher than conventional normalized ductile iron while maintaining high ductility—attributed to synergistic strengthening from ultrafine grains (1.15 μm), strong〈111〉texture, and a ternary carbide network (Mo 2 C, Mn 7 C 3 , Fe 3 C). This framework offers an efficient, generalizable pathway for on–demand design of complex alloys.

title: AI-driven X-ray CT image characterization for accelerating polymer composite design
abstract: Polymer composites offer highly tunable mechanical and thermal properties, but their design is often limited by the slow and labor-intensive characterization of microstructures from X-ray computed tomography (CT) data. An artificial intelligence (AI)-driven framework, PocomAI, is presented for rapid polymer composite characterization and generation directly from X-ray CT images. PocomAI integrates multiple deep learning models to perform image segmentation, conditional 3D voxel-grid generation, super-resolution, 3D instance segmentation, voxel-to-mesh reconstruction, and homogenized property prediction within a unified workflow. Trained on a synthetic multimodal dataset of polymer composites containing discrete particulate fillers, the framework enables rapid reconstruction of composite microstructures and prediction of filler-phase volume fraction, Young’s modulus, and thermal conductivity. The generated microstructures show good morphological and property-level consistency with reference structures. Experimental validation using X-ray CT data further demonstrates that fine-tuned PocomAI generates statistically plausible 3D microstructures from limited sliced images, with homogenization-derived effective properties consistent with those of reference reconstructions. PocomAI is further integrated with a large language model to provide a user-friendly interface for stepwise guidance, automatic tool selection, and structured outputs. By reducing post-acquisition characterization time from hours to less than one minute, PocomAI provides an efficient framework for polymer composite design.

title: Using AI to diagnose shrinkage in injection-molded products via monitoring PVT properties of amorphous polymers
abstract: Injection molding of amorphous polymers often suffers from shrinkage and warpage due to the complex rheological behavior of plastic melts, making parameter control like temperature and pressure challenging; traditionally, operators rely on trial-and-error based on experience, but this study advocates a systematic approach using sensors in the mold cavity to monitor temperature and pressure, converting data to specific volume via pressure–specific volume–temperature (PVT) relationships as a quality indicator. Employing design of experiments (DOE), the Taguchi method screens significant factors through signal-to-noise ratios, followed by response surface methodology (RSM) with central composite design (CCD) and Box–Behnken design (BBD) for optimization, while an artificial neural network (ANN) predicts quality with hyperparameters tuned by uniform design (UD). Results show the packing stage most impacts volumetric shrinkage; CCD proves more accurate than BBD due to better design point distribution, reducing shrinkage to 1.22%, with CCD's optimal packing time 0.4s shorter. ANN error decreased from 3.29% to 1.52% post-tuning, validating the method. Overall, integrating DOE and ANN effectively predicts and mitigates defects, enhancing process reliability over empirical methods.

title: Data-driven topology design and experimental validation of hyperelastic auxetic metamaterials
abstract: The design and fabrication of hyperelastic auxetic metamaterials are particularly challenging because of coupled material and geometric nonlinearities, structural instability, and internal self-contact under large deformation. These effects can cause premature buckling and reduce auxetic performance. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a data-driven topology design framework that integrates nonlinear finite element analysis with a learning-based generative model. The framework first prepares diverse auxetic candidates and evaluates their mechanical responses using a nonlinear model incorporating Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, geometric nonlinearity, and internal self-contact. High-performing designs are then selected by simultaneously minimizing the effective Poisson’s ratio and deformation asymmetry, and new candidates are generated through an iterative generation–evaluation–selection process. The optimized structure is fabricated by stereolithography using a commercial elastomeric resin and experimentally validated under quasi-static compression. Compared with an initial design candidate and a spline-like benchmark, the optimized specimen exhibits stronger auxetic behavior and lower global deformation asymmetry, maintaining measured effective Poisson’s ratios below over a broad strain range. Deformation observations further reveal coordinated unit-cell rotation followed by gradual contact-induced stiffening, resulting in symmetric and controllable deformation under large compression.

title: A linear-nonlinear coupled symbolic framework for accurate property prediction: A case study on beta transus temperature of titanium alloys
abstract: In material property prediction, linear empirical formulas lack accuracy and ignore interactions, while nonlinear ML models are black–box and overlook linear contributions. To overcome these dual drawbacks, we propose a novel linear–symbolic regression framework that constructs a dual–layer formula by simultaneously coupling linear and nonlinear terms, thereby preserving the explicit linear effects while fully accounting for complex elemental interactions. The efficacy of this method is demonstrated through a case study on the beta transus temperature prediction of titanium alloys. Extensive extrapolation tests show that our approach significantly outperforms traditional empirical formulas, linear regressions, and nonlinear ML models in terms of accuracy and generalizability on the present dataset. More importantly, this work offers a new paradigm for mining intricate nonlinear relationships in materials science without sacrificing the interpretable linear contribution of compositional features.

title: Machine-learning-empowered knowledge mining for general design rules in high-performance intermetallic compound interconnects
abstract: The continued scaling of semiconductor devices demands the development of advanced interconnect materials beyond the limitations of conventional copper. Here, we propose a Data-Model-Knowledge co-mining learning framework to accelerate the discovery of high-performance intermetallic candidates. Cohesive energy and the key figure-of-merit parameter ρ 0 ×λ were systematically curated from literature to construct robust regression models. Pareto optimality analysis was employed to balance the dual objectives of high cohesive energy and low ρ 0 ×λ enabling the identification of optimal intermetallic candidates for interconnect applications. Furthermore, interpretable machine learning enabled the extraction of key descriptors, leading to a generalizable design rule: binary alloys with a valence electron count (VE) between 7.658 and 9.035 and a cohesive energy (CoE) exceeding 5.765 eV exhibit a greater than 90% likelihood of being identified as Pareto-optimal candidates. Validation using high throughput calculations shows that 62.5% of the predicted candidates outperform the benchmark IrRu and Rh. In addition, several high-potential intermetallics − including CoOs, Co 3 Os, Co 4 Os, Rh 3 Os, Ir 4 W, Rh 3 Ir, and Rh 4 Ru − were identified as potential interconnect materials. This data–model–knowledge framework establishes a transferable paradigm for materials informatics, enabling the transformation of high-dimensional data into actionable design rules and accelerating the discovery of advanced materials across diverse systems.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived bioactive nanosystems and the design logic for antibiotic co-delivery against Helicobacter pylori
abstract: Helicobacter pylori eradication is increasingly compromised by multidrug resistance, gastric acid instability, mucus and biofilm barriers, protected bacterial niches, adverse effects and microbiome disruption. Nanotechnology enables programmable re-engineering of intragastric drug exposure through acid protection, mucus-transport modulation, stimuli-responsive release and synchronized co-delivery. Traditional Chinese Medicine–derived bioactives contribute mechanistically complementary anti-bacterial, anti-urease, anti-adhesive, anti-biofilm, anti-inflammatory and mucosa-protective functions. This Review critically appraises the evidence for combining these bioactives with antibiotics in nanocarriers: it classifies anti- Helicobacter pylori bioactives by chemical class, compiles representative nanosystems carrying Traditional Chinese Medicine bioactives with quantitative physicochemical and efficacy data, and appraises the quantitative basis of antibiotic–Traditional Chinese Medicine synergy. Crucially, genuine co-delivery—one carrier delivering a named antibiotic and a named bioactive—has not yet been achieved for Helicobacter pylori , and this Review therefore specifies what would be required to construct it. The strategy is contextualized against potassium-competitive acid blocker–based regimens and alternatives including phage and endolysin therapy, probiotics and vaccines. Translational barriers—safety, reproducibility, model validity, microbiome effects and regulatory complexity—are critically assessed, and network pharmacology and artificial intelligence–guided formulation are positioned as early-stage enablers. Clinically credible progress demands evidence-grounded platform selection, standardized quality control, predictive gastric models and rigorous clinical validation.

title: Towards high performance and long-term stability: Strategies and challenges for zirconia ceramic stabilizers
abstract: Zirconia ceramics are critical in aerospace, biomedicine, and mechanical engineering due to their high hardness, strength, biocompatibility, and chemical stability. However, their long-term reliability faces low-temperature degradation (LTD), posing an irreconcilable trade‑off among strength, toughness, and aging resistance. This paper systematically reviews recent progress across three dimensions: defect engineering and stabilization, microstructural tailoring and mechanical optimization, and multilevel LTD protection strategies. Importantly, it explores the transformative potential of artificial intelligence in breaking the trade‑off: machine learning interatomic potentials bridge first‑principles accuracy with large‑scale molecular dynamics; graph neural networks and active learning improve search efficiency in high‑dimensional compositional spaces by over an order of magnitude; and intelligent diagnostic frameworks combining nondestructive testing and deep learning enable dynamic prediction of degradation. The paper identifies that future breakthroughs hinge on the deep integration of fundamental mechanistic understanding, cross‑scale structural design, and AI‑driven rational paradigms. It also calls for standardized, open‑shared materials databases to support the shift from trial‑and‑error to data‑driven systems engineering, thereby offering a theoretical and practical roadmap for next‑generation high‑performance, long‑life zirconia‑based materials.

title: Full-field reconstruction of noisy DIC displacement fields beyond reliable measurement regions via a measurement-conditioned physics-informed neural network
abstract: This study presents a measurement-conditioned physics-informed framework for denoising digital image correlation (DIC) displacement fields within reliably measured regions and mechanically constrained completion where data are missing or unreliable. Spatial coordinates and a small number of selected DIC displacements are used as case-conditioning inputs to distinguish multiple field cases within a single network. Displacement-data fidelity constrains the measured region, while quasi-static equilibrium and boundary conditions constrain the data-excluded regions; both regions share a continuous network representation. Strain and stress fields are derived from the reconstructed displacement field through automatic differentiation and linear-elastic constitutive relations. The approach is evaluated using two finite-element-based DIC-like examples with 10% Gaussian noise and an experimental fatigue-crack-growth dataset for an AA2024-T3 M(T) specimen. The numerical examples provide clean references for quantitative assessment, while the experimental example examines applicability to measured DIC data. An ablation study comparing MSE, MAE, Huber, and Huber with self-adaptive weighting examines the influence of data-fidelity loss and adaptive point-wise weighting. The results demonstrate noise suppression within measured regions and spatial reconstruction near specimen boundaries, holes, and crack-affected regions excluded from the data-fidelity loss.

title: StampFormer: A physics-guided material-geometry-coupled multimodal model for rapid prediction of physical fields in sheet metal stamping
abstract: Traditional sheet metal forming relies on computationally expensive Finite Element Analysis (FEA), significantly prolonging design cycles. While surrogate models accelerate iteration, existing approaches either provide limited scalar outputs or ignore crucial material properties by focusing solely on geometry. To address this gap, we develop StampFormer, a physics-guided deep learning framework that simultaneously processes component geometry and material stress-strain responses to predict FEA outcomes. Its architecture employs a Material-Augmented Geometric Network (MAGN) for initial multimodal fusion, followed by a Hierarchical Material Embedding Injection Unit (HMEIU) that progressively integrates material features into an adapted Swin-UNet backbone. Evaluated on steel and aluminium crossmember stamping datasets, StampFormer predicts critical physical fields—including thinning, major/minor strain, plastic strain, and displacement—in under a second. Compared with the reference FEA, our model achieves a mean representative-maximum relative error below for each of the four 2D fields in both material datasets and a masked displacement mean squared error below mm 2 . Within the investigated component family and fixed process conditions, this multimodal framework provides sub-second predictions for rapid early-stage material–geometry screening and design exploration.

title: A dynamic mixture-of-experts framework for predicting tensile strength retention of FRP composites at elevated temperatures
abstract: Accurate prediction of tensile strength retention (TSR) of fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites exposed to elevated temperatures is essential for assessing their thermal reliability. However, existing ML approaches for TSR prediction have mainly focused on classical algorithms, while recent tabular foundation models and adaptive ensemble strategies remain unexplored. This study addresses these gaps by developing a dynamic Mixture of Experts (MOE) framework using 671 experimental results collected from 26 studies and ten materials, manufacturing, and thermal-exposure variables. Eighteen ML algorithms were systematically evaluated after preprocessing and hyperparameter optimization using grid search with 5-fold cross-validation. TabPFN achieved the best model performance on the independent test set, with an MAE of 2.960, R 2 of 96.788 %, and RMSE of 4.204. To overcome limitations of fixed ensemble methods, five high-performing algorithms (AdaBoost, CatBoost, GBM, RF, and XGBoost) were integrated as experts within a sample-specific dynamic MOE framework. Expert reliability was estimated using training-derived out-of-fold errors, enabling adaptive inverse-error-based weighting without using test target values. Evaluation of 26 expert combinations showed that MOE 1, combining AdaBoost and CatBoost, achieved an MAE of 2.629, R 2 of 96.788 %, and RMSE of 4.204. The proposed framework provides a data-driven approach for predicting thermal degradation behavior of heterogeneous FRP composites.

title: Innovative advances in intelligent droplet microfluidics: from machine vision-augmented quantifications to autonomous control
abstract: Droplet microfluidics has emerged as a powerful platform for high-throughput chemical and biological processing, offering precise control over multiphase flows, minimal reagent consumption, and scalable operation. However, accurate prediction and control of droplet formation remain fundamentally challenging because droplet breakup is governed by strongly coupled, nonlinear interactions among interfacial tension, viscous forces, flow conditions, and microchannel geometry that abruptly switch between distinct regimes. Conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and semi-empirical scaling laws not only incur prohibitive computational cost but, more critically, fail to generalize across geometries and break down for complex fluids, surfactant-laden interfaces, non-Newtonian rheology, and cannot perform the inverse design or real-time control that practical devices demand. Artificial intelligence (AI) directly addresses these intractable problems by learning high-dimensional, nonlinear mappings from data without explicit governing equations. Machine learning and deep learning predict droplet characteristics, classify flow regimes, and analyze high-speed imaging orders of magnitude faster than CFD, while reinforcement learning and Bayesian optimization enable closed-loop control and autonomous experimentation unattainable by conventional means. This review surveys AI integration across predictive modeling, intelligent flow control, and automated design, and discusses emerging opportunities and key challenges, data scarcity, model generalization, and system integration, toward autonomous, intelligent microfluidic laboratories.

title: Self-evolving digital twin with federated reinforcement learning for autonomous process–property optimization in polymer nanocomposite manufacturing systems
abstract: Rapid growth of polymer nanocomposite manufacturing demands intelligent systems capable of accurately predicting multi-property behavior and autonomously optimizing process conditions across heterogeneous industrial environments. Existing Digital Twin (DT) and machine learning approaches often suffer from centralized data dependency, limited generalization under non-IID conditions, and an inability to adaptively optimize process parameters in real time. To address these constraints, this study proposes a Self-Evolving Digital Twin framework integrating a Neural Adaptive Fusion Transformer (NAF-Transformer), FedAdam-based federated learning, and a Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) reinforcement learning agent. The model is implemented using Python, PyTorch, Gym, NumPy, and executed on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU. The system is trained on the Nanocomposites Properties Dataset (Kaggle), comprising key manufacturing inputs such as filler loading, temperature, mixing time, and curing conditions. The proposed DT demonstrates exceptional predictive performance, achieving R 2 = 0.978 and RMSE = 0.085, outperforming state-of-the-art FL–DT studies by 12–18% accuracy improvement. Federated aggregation enhances global model generalization by 10% compared to local DTs, while the TD3 agent optimizes process parameters such as temperature and mixing time, resulting in material property improvements of up to 15.3% in tensile strength, 10.2% in modulus, and 7.5% in thermal stability. The unified DT–FedAdam–TD3 architecture enables adaptive model updating, data-local federated learning, and autonomous multi-objective optimization. Overall, this study introduces a powerful, scalable, DT framework capable of continuous self-evolution, offering a significant leap beyond existing predictive or rule-based control strategies in polymer nanocomposite manufacturing.

title: Evolutionary machine learning for thermophysical property modeling and materials design of CNT–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids
abstract: Hybrid nanofluids incorporating carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and metal oxide nanoparticles have emerged as advanced functional nanomaterials for thermal management because of their tunable thermophysical properties and synergistic nanoparticle interactions. However, the strong nonlinear dependence of their density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and specific heat capacity on nanoparticle composition and concentration complicates accurate property prediction and materials design. In this study, an evolutionary machine learning framework is developed to establish composition–property relationships for aqueous CNT–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids. A multilayer perceptron neural network (MLPNN) coupled with a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to optimize the network architecture and learning parameters and to predict four key thermophysical properties, namely density, viscosity, thermal conductivity, and specific heat capacity. The predictive performance of the evolutionary GA–MLPNN model is systematically benchmarked against Gaussian process regression (GPR) and classification and regression tree (CART) models. The results demonstrate that GA–MLPNN provides highly accurate predictions for all investigated properties, achieving correlation coefficients above 0.998 for density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity and reaching 0.9999 for specific heat capacity. The analysis further reveals distinct composition–property relationships: nanoparticle volume fraction is the principal factor controlling density, viscosity, and thermal conductivity, whereas the specific heat capacity is strongly associated with the thermal capacity contributions of the constituent phases. These results demonstrate that evolutionary learning can effectively capture the complex property landscape of CNT–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids and provide an efficient route for thermophysical property estimation without extensive additional experimentation. The proposed framework establishes a materials-oriented computational strategy for screening and designing hybrid nanofluids with tailored thermophysical properties for advanced thermal-management and energy-related applications.

title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
abstract: We present a high-dimensional neural network potential (HDNNP) for the martensitic phase of the NiTi shape-memory alloy trained to density functional theory (DFT) data. A central aspect of this work is the systematic validation of the potential with respect to the underlying DFT reference method for key properties governing structural evolution, including equilibrium crystal structures, elastic constants, generalized-stacking fault energies, and vibrational spectra. The HDNNP accurately describes the relative stability of the B19$^\prime$ and B33 phases, including subtle energy differences on the order of meV/atom. The predicted stacking-fault energy landscape is strongly anisotropic and reveals a preferential shear pathway, providing atomistic insight into deformation and twinning mechanisms. Finite-temperature molecular dynamics simulations further enable the investigation of unconstrained structural evolution as a function of temperature. Overall, the developed HDNNP provides a robust basis for atomistic simulations of the complex structural and functional behavior of martensitic NiTi systems containing hundreds of thousands of atoms on nanosecond time scales.

title: Explainable machine learning framework for design and performance optimization of MOF-TFN FO membranes
abstract: The escalating need for efficient and sustainable water-treatment solutions has placed MOF-incorporated TFN FO membranes at the forefront of membrane research thanks to their notable potential for seawater desalination and wastewater treatment, largely due to their capacity for high Water Flux (Jw) coupled with suppressed Reverse Solute Flux (Js). Still, a persistent and often frustrating challenge lies in navigating the inherent trade-off between Jw and Js. In this study, we turn to machine learning (ML) for a more systematic membrane design and performance optimization strategy. Beyond prediction, we sought to open the “black box” and understand why certain membrane compositions and operating conditions lead to better outcomes. Through Pearson correlation analysis, SHAP-based feature importance, single- and two-variable PDPs, DML causal-effect heterogeneity analysis, and feature-guided uncertainty-aware stepwise PSO we identified not only which structural and operational parameters matter most, but also how they interact—sometimes in non-intuitive ways. The main contribution of this study lies in integrating all these techniques into a complete ML framework, which not only delivers robust, data-driven performance predictions for MOF-TFN FO membranes, but also provides actionable guidance for their design and optimization, reinforcing the value of ML as a tool for innovation in membrane technology

title: Cross-attentive PINN modeling of Cu-Ni interdiffusion in variable thickness Sn-2.5Ag solder joints
abstract: The aim of this study is to unravel the coupled effects of under-bump metallization (UBM) configuration, solder joint thickness, and joining sequence on interfacial intermetallic compound (IMC) formation, Cu-Ni cross-diffusion kinetics, and long-term reliability in microelectronic solder joints-a critical challenge for three-dimensional integrated circuit packaging. Symmetric Cu/Sn-2.5Ag/Cu, Ni/Sn-2.5Ag/Ni, and asymmetric Cu/Sn-2.5Ag/Ni copper pillar microbumps were fabricated and subjected to thermal cycling tests (TCTs, − 55 ∘ C to 125 ∘ C , up to 1000 cycles), with asymmetric joints processed via two pathways: Cu-first (Path I) and Ni-first (Path II). Characterization revealed (Cu,Ni) 6 Sn 5 at both interfaces in Cu-based joints, Ni 3 Sn 4 in Ni-based systems, and path- and height-dependent (Cu,Ni) 6 Sn 5 variation in asymmetric joints. Kirkendall voids formed extensively in Cu 3 Sn of symmetric Cu/Cu joints but were suppressed in asymmetric configurations, indicating superior reliability. To elucidate cross-diffusion mechanisms, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) simulated coupled solute transport in liquid solder across variable thicknesses and boundary concentrations. Building on these solutions, CuNiCrossDiffusionLLM-a transformer-inspired cross-attention interpolation framework with natural language query reasoning enabled rapid, physically consistent predictions of concentration fields, fluxes, and uphill diffusion without retraining. The framework shows that Cu-Ni cross-interaction accelerates diffusion fronts relative to self-diffusion, with thinner layers exhibiting intensified fluxes and pronounced uphill diffusion, where Cu’s steeper gradient drives stronger Ni uphill transport near zero-flux planes. These findings explain accelerated IMC growth in thinner joints and establish a digital-twin platform for parametric design, process optimization, and reliability assessment, bridging fundamental diffusion physics with engineering applications.

title: Predicting grain growth evolution under complex thermal profiles with deep learning through thermal descriptor modulation
abstract: Predicting microstructure evolution during thermomechanical treatment is essential for determining the final mechanical properties of a material, yet conventional simulations based on Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) remain computationally expensive. Our prior Deep Learning (DL) framework using Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) has proven effective in accelerating grain growth prediction, though its applicability was limited to constant-temperature or single-rate thermal profiles. As the model was trained exclusively under constant thermal conditions, it cannot account for the thermal history dependence of grain boundary kinetics, fundamentally limiting its applicability to the time-varying thermal profiles characteristic of industrial heat treatment processes. This study extends the previous framework by incorporating Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) for thermal conditioning to predict grain growth under complex, time-varying thermal profiles. The model was trained on a large dataset of grain growth evolution under thermal profiles with heating and cooling rates ranging from 0.01 kelvin per second to 10 kelvin per second. The results demonstrate that the proposed thermal conditioning mechanism enables the model to capture the influence of variable thermal profiles on grain boundary migration kinetics. Across the three test scenarios of increasing complexity, the model achieved a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of up to 0.93 and mean grain size error below 3.2%. Despite the architectural extensions, inference time remains on the order of seconds per prediction sequence, preserving the computational advantage over PDE-based simulations.

title: A machine-learning-based shear lag model for accurate analysis of the bending behavior of sandwich beams
abstract: The bending behavior of sandwich beams is significantly affected by the shear deformation of the soft core layer, which transfers normal stress between the upper and lower hard surface layers. However, due to prior assumptions about deformation distribution or difficulty in accurately describing boundary conditions, existing bending theories cannot accurately predict the mechanical behavior. In this paper, a machine-learning-based shear lag model is proposed, which aims to predict stress and deformation fields using a physics-informed neural networks method, without priori assumptions or closed-form boundary conditions. It shows that all stress and deformation predictions are in good agreement with finite element simulation results (with errors less than 10%), with better accuracy than the existing Newmark shear lag model. Furthermore, either a larger modulus difference or a smaller thickness difference between surface and core layers not only increases the normal stress in the hard surface layer, but also reduces bending stiffness, which is beneficial for improving the load transfer efficiency and toughness. Comparing with finite element results, the applicability of the model for modulus and thickness ratios of the surface/core layers is ultimately clarified. This study provides a reliable theoretical tool for guiding the design of sandwich structures with ideal properties.
